---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/uv (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv)</summary>

### [`v0.13.5`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0135)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/0.13.4...0.13.5)

Released on 2026-10-21.

Following [uv 0.13.4](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/tag/0.13.4), which removed the affected eMudhra/emSign root from uv's own certificate store, this release updates the latest managed CPython builds for 3.11 and newer to [python-build-standalone 20261021](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/tag/20261021), including the CPython [3.15.1](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3151/), [3.14.9](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3149/), and [3.13.17](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31317/) security patch releases. These builds include [pip 26.2.2](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/news/#v26-2-2) both preinstalled in the managed interpreter and bundled with `ensurepip`, which installs pip by default when you run `python -m venv`. Both copies use certifi 2026.10.19, which removes the same affected root. After upgrading uv, run `uv python upgrade` to install the updated builds. Virtual environments pinned to an older Python patch version do not switch to the updated interpreter automatically. Upgrade pip separately in existing virtual environments.

Please note upstream CPython 3.9 and 3.10 still bundle pip releases whose certificate bundles trust the affected eMudhra/emSign root. We recommend migrating off of those versions and will no longer be releasing Docker images with uv installed for EOL Python versions.

##### Enhancements

- Report incompatible self-dependencies directly in resolution errors ([#​21845](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21845))

##### Python

- Add CPython 3.15.1, 3.14.9, and 3.13.17 ([#​22802](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22802))

##### Preview features

- Select and rank wheel variants with no required properties or properties from PEP 850 static providers in platform-specific resolutions with `wheel-variants` ([#​22535](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22535), [#​22536](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22536), [#​22687](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22687), [#​22688](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22688))

##### Performance

- Reduce peak memory use when resolving dependencies across multiple environments ([#​22769](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22769), [#​22770](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22770), [#​22784](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22784))
- Speed up exports with complex transitive extras by resolving activation across the dependency graph ([#​22751](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22751))
- Reduce uv's binary size by keeping additional error formatters out of line ([#​22775](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22775))
- Reduce overhead when parsing custom build cache keys ([#​22749](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22749))

##### Bug fixes

- Lock packages distributed only as Android wheels without a source distribution ([#​22806](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22806))
- Export optional dependencies correctly when transitive extras are activated through different or incompatible environment paths ([#​22751](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22751))
- Reject invalid custom build cache keys instead of silently falling back to the defaults ([#​22749](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22749))

##### Security

- Reject certificate chains containing compromised eMudhra intermediate keys via `rustls-webpki` 0.103.16 ([#​22777](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22777))
- Stop publishing uv Docker images based on Python 3.9 and 3.10 images that no longer receive upstream updates ([#​22773](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22773))

</details>

<details>
<summary>open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases (otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib)</summary>

### [`v0.163.2`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/tag/v0.163.2)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/compare/v0.163.1...v0.163.2)

This release updates the binaries' Go version and CA bundle. It fixes [#​1722](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1722).

To see the collector changes in v0.163.x see [v0.163.0](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/tag/v0.163.0)

#### Changelog

- [`6c65793`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/commit/6c65793ec707f673304e52dfcb642684fda1a048) \[chore] Prepare release 0.163.2 ([#​1726](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1726))
- [`fb0342c`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/commit/fb0342cf6d12ea5b95697eb39564fe48b2f407df) maint: ensure we use the latest Go and CA bundles ([#​1723](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1723))
- [`94fec53`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/commit/94fec53ca1bf43dd47f180067db5675328705fde) Update golang:1.27-alpine3.23 Docker digest to [`895e5fe`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/commit/895e5fe) ([#​1720](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1720))
- [`022f629`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/commit/022f62959e0703f56ebe98df8e3801fafb60c17a) Update github-actions deps ([#​1721](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1721))

### [`v0.163.1`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v01631)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/compare/v0.162.0...v0.163.1)

### [`v0.162.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v01620)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/compare/v0.161.0...v0.162.0)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `otelcol-contrib`: Remove `wavefrontreceiver` from the contrib distribution after its deprecation period. ([#​1673](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1673))

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

- `otelcol-contrib`: Add `sdnotifyextension` to the contrib distribution. ([#​49607](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/49607))

- `otelcol-prometheus`: Create the new otelcol-prometheus distribution, which includes "Prometheus exporters" as metric receivers. ([#​1618](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1618))
  The new otelcol-prometheus distribution is a collaboration between the Prometheus and OpenTelemetry communities.
  Existing [Prometheus exporters](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exporters/) are slowly being refactored to be usable as Collector receivers in custom Collector distributions built with OCB.

  As more Prometheus exporters are refactored to be usable as Collector receivers, we will add them to the otelcol-prometheus distribution.

  The otelcol-prometheus distribution is experimental, and is not recommended for production use.

  [Build a custom Collector distribution](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/extend/ocb/) if you need components from other OpenTelemetry Collector distributions such as contrib.

- `receiver/blackbox`: Add the [Prometheus blackbox_exporter](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/blackbox_exporter) as a receiver for probe metrics in otelcol-prometheus distribution. ([#​1664](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1664))

- `receiver/postgres`: Add the [Prometheus postgres_exporter](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter) as a receiver for PostgreSQL metrics in otelcol-prometheus distribution. ([#​1664](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1664))

### [`v0.161.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v01610)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/compare/v0.160.0...v0.161.0)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `all`: Remove the deprecated mezmo exporter. ([#​49953](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/49953))
  Use the OTLP/HTTP exporter to send logs directly to Mezmo instead. See
  <https://docs.mezmo.com/telemetry-pipelines/otel-collector> and
  <https://docs.mezmo.com/telemetry-pipelines/open-telemetry-source> for migration guidance.

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `otelcol-contrib`: Upgrade go.opentelemetry.io/obi to v0.13.0 ([#​1643](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/issues/1643))

</details>

<details>
<summary>prometheus/prometheus (prom/prometheus)</summary>

### [`v3.15.1`](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/releases/tag/v3.15.1): 3.15.1 / 2026-10-21

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/compare/v3.15.0...v3.15.1)

- \[SECURITY] Container images: Update CA certificates to distrust "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" and "Comodo AAA Services root" following the compromise of eMudhra intermediate CA private keys.
- \[SECURITY] Build with Go 1.27.3 to fix vulnerabilities in `net/http`, `net/textproto`, `crypto/tls` and `html/template`.
- \[SECURITY] Bump golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 to fix HTTP/2 vulnerabilities (GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6612, GO-2026-6617).

### [`v3.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/releases/tag/v3.15.0): 3.15.0 / 2026-09-24

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/compare/v3.14.0...v3.15.0)

- \[CHANGE] PromQL: A range query whose `end` was not aligned to `step` caused subqueries inside it to evaluate past the parent's last actual step, inflating `peakSamples` in the query stats and against the `query.max-samples` limit, and wasting storage I/O reading samples that were never used in the result. Add tests to prevent regression of the fix made in [#​18081](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18081). [#​18598](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18598)
- \[CHANGE] PromQL: Do not register a start timestamp reset if the start timestamp hasn't changed between subsequent samples. [#​19454](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19454)
- \[CHANGE] Logging: Deprecate `--log.level`; use `runtime.log_level` configuration to supply the default level. [#​19511](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19511)
- \[FEATURE] Configuration: Allow changing the process log level through `runtime.log_level` on configuration reload. [#​19511](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19511)
- \[FEATURE] Prometheus: Add `--auto-gomemlimit.refresh-interval` flag to periodically re-detect the container or system memory limit and update `GOMEMLIMIT` at runtime. [#​18843](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18843)
- \[FEATURE] Scraping: Add support for scraping targets via Unix Domain Sockets. [#​12024](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/12024). [#​18091](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18091)
- \[FEATURE] scrape: Implement OM2.0 scrape format. [#​18606](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18606)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] Reduce TSDB head CPU utilization when initializing. [#​18001](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18001)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] Docker SD: Add labels `__meta_docker_container_image` and `__meta_docker_container_image_id`. [#​19386](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19386)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] Mixin: Add a p95/p99 remote-write send-batch latency panel to the remote-write dashboard. [#​19500](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19500)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] Mixin: Support native histograms in the remote-write send-batch latency panel. [#​19522](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19522)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] PromQL/TSDB: The `--enable-feature=st-storage` flag now automatically enables XOR2 float chunk encoding and ST-capable histogram chunk encoding, so you no longer need to pass `xor2-encoding` and `histograms-st-encoding` alongside it. [#​19518](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19518)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] Remote write / Alertmanager: upgrade sigv4 to v0.5.0, adding `session_name` and `tags` fields for STS AssumeRole sessions. The previously undocumented `service_name` field is now also documented. [#​19569](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19569)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] Scraping: Support zstd-compressed scrape responses, enabled via feature flag `zstd-scrape`. [#​19502](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19502)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] TSDB: Stabilize the XOR2 float chunk encoding. `--enable-feature=xor2-encoding` is deprecated; use `storage.tsdb.chunk_encoding.floats: xor2` instead. Check that other software reading the TSDB directly (e.g. Thanos sidecar) supports XOR2 before enabling. [#​19461](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19461)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] TSDB: add `prometheus_tsdb_head_appenders_created_total` metric. [#​19411](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19411)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] Tracing: add more spans to scrapes, API queries and rule evaluations. [#​19410](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19410)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] UI: Show the effective configuration for each scrape pool on the Targets and Service Discovery pages. [#​19384](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19384)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] scrape: Enable start time synthesis for summary `_count` and `_sum` series in scrape appender v2. [#​19323](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19323)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] scrape: stop all pools in parallel for faster shutdowns. [#​19295](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19295)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] storage/remote: Add undocumented failed_request_logging config field to debug log remote write V2 requests on send errors. [#​19249](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19249)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] TSDB: Add fast path for XOR chunk decompression to speed up queries. [#​18049](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18049)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] UI: Improve native histogram table formatting and add a background bar indicating the bucket count. [#​19332](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19332)

- \[PERF] scrape: conversion from classic to native histograms should only parse start times when enabled. [#​19446](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19446)
- \[BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix `info()` enrichment for composite expressions with mixed `@`/offset references or selector-free vector branches, preventing metadata from being evaluated at an unrelated timestamp. [#​19387](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19387)

- \[BUGFIX] PromQL: Preserve metric-name dropping through the info function when delayed name removal is enabled. [#​19413](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19413)

- \[BUGFIX] TSDB: Do not retain head series after a synthetic start-timestamp zero sample is rejected. [#​19470](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19470)
- \[BUGFIX] TSDB: Prevent query panics during series eviction after WAL replay. [#​19664](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19664)
- \[BUGFIX] TSDB: fix potential deadlock between mmapSeriesChunks and gcSeries. [#​19460](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19460)
- \[BUGFIX] TSDB: fix default block reload interval for custom options. [#​19368](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19368)
- \[BUGFIX] AWS SD: Do not crash on serverless MSK clusters or MSK clusters without Open Monitoring. [#​19194](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19194)
- \[BUGFIX] AWS SD: Do not panic when the ElastiCache API omits optional fields of a serverless cache or cache cluster. [#​19435](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19435)
- \[BUGFIX] AWS SD: Reject non-positive `request_concurrency` instead of hanging service discovery indefinitely. [#​19524](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19524)
- \[BUGFIX] Discovery/AWS: Avoid a panic when discovering standalone ECS tasks with custom task groups. [#​19302](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19302)
- \[BUGFIX] Discovery: Do not panic in AWS Lightsail service discovery when an instance is missing optional fields such as availability zone, blueprint, bundle, name, state or support code. [#​19324](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19324)
- \[BUGFIX] Discovery: delete the stale `prometheus_sd_last_update_timestamp_seconds` series for a config that is removed on reload. [#​19131](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19131)
- \[BUGFIX] HTTP: Avoid truncating compressed responses when handlers set Content-Length. [#​19661](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19661)
- \[BUGFIX] IONOS SD: Do not panic when the API response omits the server, NIC or volume collections, or a server's properties. [#​19438](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19438)
- \[BUGFIX] Metadata will not affect the number of Remote Write v2 shards. [#​19218](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19218)
- \[BUGFIX] Mixins: Fix label mismatches that prevented PrometheusHAGroupNotIngestingSamples and PrometheusHAGroupCrashlooping from firing. [#​19444](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19444)
- \[BUGFIX] Native histograms: `DetectReset` no longer misses a counter reset when a populated bucket behind an empty one disappears, which could make histogram `rate()`/`increase()` undercount. [#​19367](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19367)

- \[BUGFIX] OTLP: Do not abort an entire OTLP payload ingestion if one metric has no datapoints. [#​19343](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19343)
- \[BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix FastRegexMatcher false-positive match when a capturing group is directly adjacent to a literal (e.g. `.*\|(foo)\|.*`). [#​19516](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19516)

- \[BUGFIX] PromQL: Preserve parentheses around duration literals on Expr.String() round-trip. [#​19403](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19403)
- \[BUGFIX] PromQL: Reject duration-expression offsets and `@ start()` / `@ end()` before range selectors, matching the existing rejection of literal offsets and `@ <timestamp>`. [#​19406](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19406)
- \[BUGFIX] PromQL: Report the position of the histogram argument rather than of a scalar argument in the native histogram NaN observation annotations of `histogram_quantile` and `histogram_fraction`. [#​19330](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19330)
- \[BUGFIX] PromQL: info() now applies the @​ modifier/offset when evaluating the info series, so info(v @​ T) enriches as of T consistently instead of depending on the query start/eval time. [#​19266](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19266)
- \[BUGFIX] Rules: Fix a panic when a rule manager created without a logger loads a rule file containing multiple YAML documents. [#​19433](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19433)
- \[BUGFIX] Scrape: Do not append a stale marker for a series that is still exposed when the storage returns a new series reference for it. [#​19328](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19328)
- \[BUGFIX] Scrape: JSON log formatter correctly format scrape target info. [#​19472](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19472)
- \[BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix in-order chunk ID overflow by wrapping head chunk IDs modulo 2^23 so they never collide with the out-of-order flag bit. [#​19450](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19450)
- \[BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix out-of-order chunk ID overflow by wrapping `firstOOOChunkID` modulo 2^23 instead of growing unbounded. [#​19216](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/19216)

### setuptools: MANIFEST.in exclusion bypass in sdist via Unicode normalization collision (NFC/NFD) on macOS APFS/HFS+
[CVE-2026-59890](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-59890) / [GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

When building a source distribution (`python -m build --sdist` / `setup.py sdist`), setuptools' `FileList` applies `MANIFEST.in` directives (`exclude`, `global-exclude`, `recursive-exclude`, `prune`) by matching a compiled glob against on-disk file names **byte-for-byte, with no Unicode normalization**. On normalization-preserving filesystems (notably macOS APFS and HFS+), a file written in NFD and a `MANIFEST.in` rule written in NFC refer to the same file but are byte-distinct, so the exclusion silently fails to match. A file the maintainer intended to exclude is then packed into the `.tar.gz` and, if published, uploaded to the public, immutable PyPI index.

##### Details

File names in `FileList.files` come from `os.walk` (`setuptools/_distutils/filelist.py`, `_find_all_simple`), so on APFS a file written NFD is offered to the matcher in NFD, while the `MANIFEST.in` pattern carries the author's editor form (typically NFC). The matching path performs no canonicalization:

```python

##### setuptools/command/egg_info.py  (FileList.global_exclude)
def global_exclude(self, pattern):
    match = translate_pattern(os.path.join('**', pattern))   # fnmatch.translate -> regex, no NFC/NFD
    return self._remove_files(match.match)                   # byte-level regex over raw os.walk names
```

A rule written NFC (`café` = `63 61 66 c3 a9`) does not match an on-disk name written NFD (`café` = `63 61 66 65 cc 81`), even though the filesystem treats the two as one file.

A `unicodedata.normalize('NFD', ...)` helper exists in `setuptools/unicode_utils.py` (`decompose()`), but it is **never called in the manifest matching path**, so neither the pattern nor the walked path is normalized before matching. The only normalization in this area, `EggInfoCommand._manifest_normalize`, uses `filesys_decode` (bytes→str decode only, no NFC/NFD) and runs when writing `SOURCES.txt`, after matching has already occurred.

##### Impact

`MANIFEST.in` exclusions are the documented mechanism maintainers use to keep secrets, local configs, and private fixtures out of the published sdist. A non-ASCII excluded file may be published to the public, immutable PyPI index despite the rule — an irreversible disclosure with no visual cue (NFC and NFD forms render identically). Exposure is filesystem-dependent and most relevant on macOS APFS/HFS+, where many maintainers build and publish. Pure-ASCII rules are unaffected.

##### Proof of concept

With a project containing `MANIFEST.in`:

```
global-include *.txt *.json
global-exclude secret_café.txt    # rule saved NFC
```

and an on-disk file `secret_café.txt` written in NFD, `python -m build --sdist` packs the secret file into the resulting `.tar.gz`, while an ASCII control file excluded by the same directive is correctly dropped — isolating the bypass to the NFC-pattern vs. NFD-name mismatch. Reproduced on macOS APFS with setuptools 82.0.1.

##### Remediation

Normalize both the walked path and each `MANIFEST.in` pattern to a single canonical form before matching, in both `setuptools/command/egg_info.py` (`FileList`) and the vendored `setuptools/_distutils/filelist.py`. For an exclusion list, err toward excluding more, and document that `MANIFEST.in` matching is normalization-insensitive on macOS.

##### Credit

Reported by Tomas Illuminati. Coordinated via CERT/CC VINCE VU#604762.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.1 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`

### setuptools: Windows path escape via namespace_packages.txt during legacy wheel installation  Description
[GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

On Windows, attacker-controlled content in a wheel's
`.dist-info/namespace_packages.txt` can cause setuptools' legacy wheel
installation path to create an `__init__.py` outside the requested
`destination_eggdir`.

The attacker can influence the destination path, but not the contents of
the created file.

##### Details

Tested setuptools commit:

`6ead555c5fb29bc57fe6105b1bffc163f56fd558`

Relevant source:

`setuptools/wheel.py`

SHA-256:

`359b7e0d5dd8c3135653abe08a8ed5dc0352eadfd7df22cb5e2b5303b7c3cafd`

The relevant call path is:

`Wheel(wheel_path).install_as_egg(destination)`
→ `_install_as_egg`
→ `_convert_metadata`
→ `_fix_namespace_packages`

A wheel can provide attacker-controlled content in:

`<distribution>.dist-info/namespace_packages.txt`

The namespace value is eventually used approximately as:

```python
mod_dir = os.path.join(destination_eggdir, *mod.split('.'))
mod_init = os.path.join(mod_dir, '__init__.py')

If mod is a Windows drive-qualified absolute path containing no dots,
mod.split('.') preserves it as a single component.
On Windows, os.path.join(destination_eggdir, absolute_component) discards
the original base directory and resolves to the attacker-supplied absolute
path.
The existing wheel filename and ZIP traversal checks do not validate this
metadata value before it is subsequently interpreted as a filesystem path.

```markdown

##### PoC

The reproduction was performed entirely inside a disposable temporary
directory.

Layout:

```text
sandbox/
    destination/
    outside/
    input/
    canary.txt
```

A synthetic wheel was created containing:

`demo_pkg-1.0.dist-info/namespace_packages.txt`

whose content was the absolute path of:

`sandbox\outside`

The real acquired setuptools implementation was then invoked:

```python
setuptools.wheel.Wheel(synthetic_wheel).install_as_egg(
    sandbox_destination
)
```

The operation completed without exception.

Expected metadata was created under:

`sandbox\destination\EGG-INFO`

but setuptools also created:

`sandbox\outside\__init__.py`

The file did not exist before execution.

Its contents were:

```python
__import__('pkg_resources').declare_namespace(__name__)
```

The unrelated canary remained byte-identical.

The sandbox was deleted after recording the evidence.
```

##### Impact

A crafted wheel can cause setuptools to create a fixed-content
`__init__.py` outside the intended installation directory at a
filesystem path influenced by the wheel, with the permissions of the
process performing the installation.

The demonstrated reproduction required the target parent directory to
already exist.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 1.0 / 10 (Low)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:A/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

title: Don't retry generator tasks when the finalizer fails during early close
body:
closes #23592

This PR stops a generator task from starting its body again when the consumer closes it early and its finalizer raises. Before this change, a task with `retries=1` ran its body two times, so side effects occurred two times.

Stacked on #23375. Follow-up to [this review comment](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23375#discussion_r4367696088).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The engine sets `_is_closing_generator` when it gets `GeneratorExit`. `handle_retry` (sync and async) does not retry while this flag is set.
- The engine closes the user generator (`gen.close()` / `await gen.aclose()`) before it records success, then re-raises `GeneratorExit`. If the finalizer raises, the normal exception path records the failure without a retry.
- The sync and async paths have the same change.
- This PR does not change transaction or rollback behavior. The final state for a failed finalizer stays `Failed`, as before the retry occurred.

Tests: `test_generator_closed_early_with_failing_finalizer_does_not_retry` (sync) and `test_generator_task_closed_early_with_failing_finalizer_does_not_retry` (async). Each test makes sure the body starts one time, cleanup runs one time in task context, and the task run is `Failed`.

`uv run pytest tests/test_task_engine.py tests/test_tasks.py -n4`: 571 passed.
</details>

title: Scope prefect-azure setuptools cap to AzureML extras
body:
Unblocks https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23583 (setuptools 80.10.2 → 84.1.0).

### Summary

`prefect-azure` declared an unconditional `setuptools` runtime cap (`<81` on PyPI, `<82` in source) so that `pkg_resources` stayed importable for `azureml-core`, which imports it at runtime on older supported versions (see #13672, #20617). Because AzureML is an optional extra, ordinary `prefect-azure` installs were inheriting that cap — and with setuptools 84.1 published, resolvers downgrade `prefect-azure` all the way to 0.4.8 to satisfy it.

This PR moves the cap to `setuptools<81` on the extras that actually install AzureML:

- `ml_datastore` extra: `azureml-core` + `setuptools<81`
- `all_extras` extra: same
- `dev` dependency group (which installs `azureml-core`): `setuptools<81`

Base runtime dependencies no longer mention setuptools. Build-system requirements and all other dependency minimums are unchanged.

### Verification (Python 3.12)

- Built wheel metadata: `Requires-Dist: setuptools<81` appears only under `extra == "ml-datastore"` and `extra == "all-extras"` markers — asserted by a new regression test.
- Resolution: `uv pip install 'prefect-azure[ml-datastore]' 'setuptools==84.1'` correctly fails as unsatisfiable; `ml-datastore` alone selects setuptools 80.10.2; base + `setuptools==84.1` resolves cleanly.
- Import smoke: `prefect_azure` and all non-ML modules (`credentials`, `blob_storage`, `cosmos_db`, `container_instance`, `workers.container_instance`, `repository`, `plugins`) import with setuptools 84.1 installed and `pkg_resources` absent. These are smoke tests only — they verify imports, not live Azure calls.
- Full `prefect-azure` suite (192 tests, with `azure-storage-blob`, `azure-cosmos`, and `azureml-core` installed via the dev group): all pass.
- The root `prefect[azure]` extra (`prefect-azure>=0.4.0`, no extras) will not select ML extras or a setuptools cap once a release with this change is published.

### Regression coverage

New `tests/test_packaging.py` asserts:

- base `dependencies` contain no setuptools requirement;
- `ml_datastore` / `all_extras` / the dev group carry `setuptools<81` alongside `azureml-core`;
- the built wheel's `Requires-Dist` metadata scopes setuptools to the ML extras only;
- base modules import with `pkg_resources` blocked.

### Limitations

- **A corrected `prefect-azure` release must be published before #23583 can land.** `uv.lock` resolves `prefect-azure` from PyPI (currently 0.4.13, which still carries the unconditional cap), so the dependabot PR can only be relocked against setuptools 84.1 after a release containing this fix is out. This PR intentionally does not touch `uv.lock`.
- `prefect_azure.deployments.steps` imports `azure.storage.blob` unconditionally, so it still requires the `blob_storage` extra — unchanged by this PR.
- Credential-dependent tests (live Blob/Cosmos/ACI/AML calls) were not run; coverage here is unit tests plus import smoke tests.

- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed. — packaging metadata only; no docs changes needed.

title: Bump filelock from 3.25.2 to 4.2.1
body:
Bumps [filelock](https://github.com/tox-dev/py-filelock) from 3.25.2 to 4.2.1.
Release notes

Sourced from filelock's releases.

4.2.1

  • On a singleton wrapper, close> and close> end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. #832
  • ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. #833
  • Fix ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. SQLite now opens the database by name only in a directory no other account can write, and through a private hard link elsewhere. On Windows the directory's access control list decides. Where hard links are unavailable, keep the database in a directory other accounts cannot write, such as one under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The lock removes link directories through a checked descriptor rather than by name, reads a link directory's name only when the locking account owns it, and leaves alone a directory with other content renamed onto a link directory's name. A database whose schema takes more than a few kilobytes to load raises ValueError instead of running past the acquire timeout. #834
  • Fix five bugs in opening the lock file. UnixFileLock no longer truncates a file it did not create, such as one renamed to the lock path, and no longer applies mode to it. An on_acquired hook that writes holder metadata now truncates the file itself. A lease (Linux) or an oplock (Windows) on the lock file or a soft lock's marker no longer holds acquire() past its timeout or blocking=False, and an oplock no longer holds release(); ReadWriteLock on Windows waits for its timeout and raises Timeout. On Windows, a mode without group and other bits, such as 0o600, now creates the lock file with an owner-only permission list; the ReadWriteLock database gets the same. The soft locks' writability check no longer follows a symlink swapped in at the lock path. On a filesystem without flock, a contender from another account now waits on a marker it cannot write instead of raising PermissionError. #835
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing a live holder's marker in three cases: the holder and the contender run in Linux time namespaces with different boottime offsets; only one of them can read the boot id; a process other than the owner rewrote the marker. Soft markers no longer carry group or other write bits. A process name containing a carriage return or another line separator no longer makes the stale check raise ValueError. When /proc/self/ns/time exists but cannot be read, the stale check no longer compares start times and keeps the marker. #836
  • The async read-write locks record their hold under a task owner, so synchronous code on the executor thread that took the hold can no longer re-enter or release it. AsyncSoftReadWriteLock gives back one level on release, so synchronous readers of a shared singleton keep theirs. SoftReadWriteLock tracks read levels per thread: release() from a thread that holds none raises RuntimeError. After its heartbeat recorded a lost hold, it refuses new acquires until that hold is released. #838
  • StrictSoftFileLock creates <path>.filelock and its claims directory with the lock's mode and sets the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it) on both. On the next acquisition it narrows a directory it owns that an earlier release created wider; it leaves a directory of another account as it is, so remove such leftovers by hand. It reaches claims through a descriptor opened without following symlinks; on Windows it holds both directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). Under a sticky parent such as /tmp it refuses a coordination directory of another account, as SoftReadWriteLock does for <path>.rw. One read grace now covers a whole claim scan, a failed claim cleanup no longer leaves the sentinel descriptor open, and a non-regular node at a sentinel private-record name raises SoftFileLockProtocolError. On Windows, contenders read claims without blocking their owner's unlink. #839

... (truncated)

title: Bump fast-uri from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9 in /ui-v2
body:
Bumps [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri) from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9.
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v8.12.2...v8.12.3

v8.12.2

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

title: fix(ui-v2): filter events E2E tests by exact resource IDs to avoid pagination overflow
body:
This PR fixes the flaky "Events timeline shows events from multiple resource types" E2E test. The test failed on main in [run 40144465590](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40144465590).

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

The test emits its events 2 minutes in the past. Then it filters the events page with `[flowRunResourceId, "prefect.deployment.", "prefect.work-pool."]`. The UI sends these values as `any_resource.id_prefix`. Thus the two broad prefixes match all deployment and work-pool events on the server.

Other spec files that run in parallel in the same shard create deployments. Their events are newer than the backdated test events. The page shows only 50 events (DESC order), so the test events go off the first page. The CI trace shows the problem: the `/api/events/filter` response had `total: 70`, and the first 50 events were `prefect.deployment.created` events from deployment tests. The flow-run event was not on the page.

The fix keeps the deployment and work-pool resource IDs in constants. The filter now uses the exact IDs. The "Filter by event type" test had the same filter, so this PR changes it too.

**Verification**
- Reproduced locally: I emitted 80 newer `prefect.deployment.created` noise events. The old test then failed every time.
- With the same noise and the fix, `npx playwright test e2e/events/ --repeat-each=5 --workers=1` passed (75/75).
- `biome check` passes.

</details>

title: Fix flaky events E2E tests: filter by exact resource IDs
body:
This PR fixes the flaky `Events List Page` E2E tests "Events timeline shows events from multiple resource types" and "Filter by event type". These tests failed on main in [run 40144138487](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40144138487) (shard 2/3).

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

The two tests filter the events page by resource to keep their events on the first page (limit 50, DESC order). The filter had the exact flow-run ID, but it also had the broad prefixes `"prefect.deployment."` and `"prefect.work-pool."`. The UI sends these values as `any_resource.id_prefix`, so the filter matches every deployment and work-pool event that other tests in the shard emit. The test events have an `occurred` time 2 minutes in the past. More than 50 newer deployment events push them off the first page. The CI failure screenshots show this: the page shows "3 resources selected" and lists only `Deployment Created` / `Flow Run Scheduled` events from other specs.

The fix gives the deployment and work-pool test events fixed UUID resource IDs and uses these exact IDs in the resource filter. Other tests' events can no longer match the filter.

**Local verification**
- Reproduced the failure on `main`: I emitted 100 `prefect.deployment.created` noise events (occurred 70s ago, which is inside the UI query window and newer than the test events), then ran the tests. "Events timeline shows events from multiple resource types" failed the same way as in CI.
- With this fix and the same noise before each run: the two target tests passed 20/20 times, and the full `events.spec.ts` passed 5/5 times (15/15 tests each run).
- `npx biome check e2e/` is clean.

</details>

body:
Follow-up to #23555, addressing [Codex review feedback](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23555#discussion_r4368986123). This PR changes the `test-projects/` guidance in `tests/AGENTS.md` to recommend `shutil.copytree` with `ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__")`. A plain copy keeps any `__pycache__` that another xdist worker already wrote into the source project, so assertions on directory contents can still flake. This matches the `tree_project` fixture in `tests/test_filesystems.py`.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `tests/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: In the existing `test-projects/` bullet, replace `(`shutil.copytree`)` with `(`shutil.copytree` with `ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__")`)`
Non-obvious evidence: Copying first doesn't help if another worker already wrote caches into the source directory. Only the `tree_project` fixture in `tests/test_filesystems.py` handles this case.
Cross-cutting scope: Applies to any test that uses `TEST_PROJECTS_DIR` and checks which files a project contains.
Why not code comment/docstring: `TEST_PROJECTS_DIR` is defined separately in each module, so there's no shared definition to attach a comment to.

title: docs: add whenever import guard rule to src/prefect AGENTS.md
body:
This PR is a follow-up to #23570. It adds the `whenever` import-guard rule to `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`. Agents that edit files in `src/prefect/` load that file. They do not load `client/AGENTS.md`, so the rule from #23570 did not apply to the files that it protects (from a [Codex review comment](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23570#discussion_r4368974637)). The packaging details stay in `client/AGENTS.md`.

The change adds one sentence to the existing `whenever` compat-helper bullet. The net line change is zero.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "`prefect-client` depends on `whenever` only on Python 3.13+, so modules it ships must keep `whenever` imports behind `sys.version_info >= (3, 13)`; only server code that the client build strips may import it unconditionally (see `client/AGENTS.md`)."
Non-obvious evidence: Since #23205, the root `pyproject.toml` lists `whenever` with no marker, and `server/schemas/schedules.py` imports it unconditionally. Dev installs always include `whenever`, so repo tests do not find an unguarded import in client-side code. Only the Python 3.11 `prefect-client` smoke tests can find it, and only for code paths that they import.
Cross-cutting scope: All modules under `src/prefect/` that go into `prefect-client`.
Why not code comment/docstring: The mistake is a new import in any module. No single module comment is the right place. The existing `whenever` rule in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` is where agents look for this guidance.
Durability: It stays true while the client marker `python_version>='3.13'` differs from the root dependency.
Counter-evidence checked: `client/AGENTS.md` (has the rule from #23570, but it is outside the ancestor scope of `src/prefect/`), the existing `whenever` bullet in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` (says "on Python 3.13+" but does not give the reason), `types/_datetime.py` (has the guards but does not explain them), `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py`.

</details>

title: docs: document tolerant reads of unknown automation values
body:
This PR adds one bullet to the Key Contracts section of `src/prefect/events/AGENTS.md`. The bullet tells agents that client automation schemas must read action types and metric names that this version does not know. It also tells agents that code which reads automations must handle these unknown variants.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/events/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**Automation schemas must read values this version doesn't know.** Cloud can add action types and metric names before a client release knows about them, so unknown actions parse as `UnknownAction` and unknown metric names stay `str` in `MetricTriggerQuery.name`. Code that reads automations must handle these variants (e.g. no `.value` on a metric name without an `isinstance` check), and `prefect transfer` skips automations that use them instead of copying them."
Non-obvious evidence: `MetricTriggerQuery.name` looks like a `PrefectMetric` enum, but it can be a plain `str`. `MetricTrigger.describe` used `m.name.value` and had to change in #23513. The docstring on `UnknownAction` and the inline comment on `MetricTriggerQuery.name` each explain one field. No document states the shared rule or the consumer obligation.
Cross-cutting scope: Client automation schemas (`events/actions.py`, `events/schemas/automations.py`), all code that reads automations (CLI display, `prefect transfer`), and new Cloud-extensible fields added in the future. The same pattern landed in three PRs (#23426, #23448, #23513).
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to consumers in other packages (for example `cli/transfer/`) and to schema fields that do not exist yet. A docstring on one model does not reach these places.
Durability: Cloud will continue to add action types and metrics before client releases. The tolerant-read contract and the consumer obligation stay valid while the client reads Cloud automations.
Counter-evidence checked: `UnknownAction` docstring, inline comment on `MetricTriggerQuery.name`, `cli/transfer/_migratable_resources/automations.py` comments, `tests/events/client/test_automations_schema.py`, `tests/cli/transfer/test_automations.py`, `src/prefect/events/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`. None of them state the shared rule.

</details>

title: docs: document whenever dependency split in client AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds one contract to `client/AGENTS.md`. After #23205, `prefect` needs `whenever` on all Python versions. `prefect-client` still needs it only on Python 3.13+. Code that goes into `prefect-client` must keep its `whenever` imports behind a version guard.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `client/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "`whenever` is required by `prefect` on all Pythons but by `prefect-client` only on 3.13+. Server-only code (e.g. `server/schemas/schedules.py`) may import it unconditionally; code shipped in `prefect-client` must keep it behind `sys.version_info >= (3, 13)` like `types/_datetime.py`. Repo tests won't catch a violation because dev installs always include `whenever`. Marker-only differences like this must be allowlisted explicitly in `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py`."
Non-obvious evidence: The root `pyproject.toml` now lists `whenever` with no marker. A developer who looks at it, or at the unconditional `import whenever` in `server/schemas/schedules.py`, can think it is safe to import `whenever` anywhere. But `client/pyproject.toml` keeps `python_version>='3.13'`. The full test suite always has `whenever` installed, so it does not find this mistake. Only the Python 3.11 `prefect-client` smoke tests in CI can find it, and only for code paths that they import.
Cross-cutting scope: All modules in `src/prefect/` that go into `prefect-client` (everything except stripped server/CLI code). It also applies to the dependency-mirroring check in `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py`.
Why not code comment/docstring: The contract connects the root `pyproject.toml`, `client/pyproject.toml`, `build_client.sh` strip rules, and any client-side module. No single file is the right place for it. `client/AGENTS.md` already owns the "mirror dependencies" contract that this refines.
Durability: It stays true while the marker split exists. The split continues until `prefect-client` drops support for Python < 3.13, or the client starts to need `whenever` on all versions.
Counter-evidence checked: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` (the `whenever` compat-helper rule says "on Python 3.13+" but does not mention the packaging split), root `AGENTS.md` (general dependency-mirroring rule), `client/AGENTS.md` (general mirroring and server-import rules), the comment in `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py` (it explains the exception but not the import rule for client code), `.github/workflows/prefect-client.yaml` (smoke tests run on Python 3.11 only).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in triggering push (4bc9bbcffe61cfdb2bf3d44e0f1a93dfbbd196ea..a9452ac21852755311913cb27887b083b5007c03)</summary>

- `pyproject.toml`
- `src/prefect/server/schemas/schedules.py`
- `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py`
- `tests/server/schemas/test_schedules.py`
- `uv.lock`

</details>

title: docs: document SQLAlchemy minor-version contract in server AGENTS.md
body:
this PR adds one Key Contracts bullet to `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`: server code must run on every SQLAlchemy minor allowed by `pyproject.toml` (currently 2.0 and 2.1), even though CI only tests the version locked in `uv.lock`.

Follow-up to #23201, where SQLAlchemy 2.1 broke deployment scheduling on fresh installs while CI (locked to 2.0.45) stayed green.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**Server code must run on every SQLAlchemy minor allowed by `pyproject.toml` (currently 2.0 and 2.1)** — CI only tests the version locked in `uv.lock`, and tests turn `SADeprecationWarning` into errors, so newer-minor breakage surfaces only on fresh installs. Avoid APIs deprecated in the newest minor (e.g. `Result.t`, `orm.noload`, PostgreSQL `Select.distinct(expr)`); feature-detect where versions diverge (see `distinct_on` in `database/query_components.py`). Check with `uv run --with 'sqlalchemy[asyncio]==<newest>' pytest tests/server`."
Non-obvious evidence: `pyproject.toml` allows `sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0,<3.0.0` but `uv.lock` pins 2.0.45 and no CI workflow tests a newer SQLAlchemy, so an agent validating locally/CI never sees 2.1 failures. `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]` only ignores `SAWarning`, not `SADeprecationWarning`, which is easy to miss.
Cross-cutting scope: All server ORM/query code (`models/`, `database/`, `api/`, `schemas/filters.py`) on both SQLite and PostgreSQL — #23201 touched five unrelated modules for the same root cause.
Why not code comment/docstring: The constraint spans every query site; the single inline comment next to `distinct_on` only explains that one call site, not the general contract or the CI gap.
Durability: Holds as long as the dependency range spans more than the locked minor, which is the normal state between lockfile bumps; the "currently 2.0 and 2.1" parenthetical is the only part that ages.
Counter-evidence checked: Existing `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md` (only mentions SQLAlchemy as the model layer), root `AGENTS.md` (lists SQLAlchemy 2.0 in the tech stack, no compatibility guidance), `tests/AGENTS.md`, `pyproject.toml` filterwarnings, `.github/workflows/` (no SQLAlchemy version matrix), and the inline comments added in #23201.

</details>

- src/prefect/server/api/ui/flow_runs.py

title: docs: document cross-resource query invalidation in ui-v2 api AGENTS.md
body:
this PR adds cross-resource cache invalidation to the ui-v2 API mutation guidelines.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: ui-v2/src/api/AGENTS.md
Proposed text: Under Mutation Guidelines > invalidation, add a "Cross-resource" bullet: if a mutation changes data cached under another resource's key factory (e.g. deployment create/delete changes `flows` `deploymentsCount`), also invalidate that factory's prefix key — the mutated resource's `all()` does not cover it.
Non-obvious evidence: The existing guidelines only cover invalidating the mutated resource's own `lists()`/`counts()`/`detail()`. Derived counts cached under a different resource's factory went stale (fixed in #23354 by adding `flowsQueryKeyFactory.deploymentsCounts()` invalidation); no comment in `deployments/index.ts` explains this.
Cross-cutting scope: Applies to every mutation hook in `ui-v2/src/api/` whose effects show up in another resource's cached queries (already used by deployments → flows and block-documents → admin).
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule governs how future mutation hooks are written across resources, not any single hook's behavior.
Durability: Query key factories are per-resource by convention, so cross-resource derived data will keep coming up as the React UI migration adds views.
Counter-evidence checked: ui-v2/src/api/AGENTS.md, ui-v2/AGENTS.md, ui-v2/src/components/AGENTS.md, ui-v2/src/hooks/AGENTS.md, `deployments/index.ts`, `flows/index.ts`, `deployments.test.ts`.

title: Ignore Python 3.15 fork-with-threads warning in `test_forked_child_exits_cleanly_with_running_service`
body:
This PR adds a `filterwarnings` mark to `test_forked_child_exits_cleanly_with_running_service` so that the test passes on Python 3.15.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The test was added in #23464. It forks a child process while `MockService` and the global event loop threads run. That is the purpose of the test.

On Python 3.15, `os.fork()` in a multi-threaded process emits `DeprecationWarning: This process (pid=...) is multi-threaded, use of fork() may lead to deadlocks in the child.` Our pytest config sets `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]`, so the warning becomes an error. On Python 3.15 the failure is deterministic, not flaky. The `Client Tests: Modules - python:3.15` job failed on every `main` run since #23464 merged:
- https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40108528899 (e81524ab05)
- https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40110045754 (c385b50dd0)
- https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40110052056 (d296bc008d)

The fix uses the same ignore filter as `test_manager_has_lock_information_when_deserialized_in_new_process_with_fork` in `tests/test_locking.py`.

Local verification on Python 3.15.1:
- Before the fix: the test fails with the same `DeprecationWarning`.
- After the fix: the test passes in 20 of 20 runs. The full `tests/_internal/concurrency/test_services.py` module passes on 3.15 and on 3.12 with `-n4`.

title: docs: document search-keyed query exception in ui-v2 AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds one bullet to the "API Integration" section of `ui-v2/AGENTS.md`. The bullet tells agents not to use `useSuspenseQuery` for queries whose key changes as the user types in a search or filter input. A new key suspends the tree again. This remounts the input, and the input loses focus. The bullet tells agents to use `useQuery` with `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` for these queries. It also tells agents to get filtered counts from the paginated response.

Before this change, the section said "Use `useSuspenseQuery` over `useQuery`" and gave only one exception. Agents who follow that rule cause this bug again. The bug occurred three times: #19827 (events feed), #22497 (deployments), and #23338 (flows).

The audit also looked at the runner change in #23346 (SIGTERM now schedules `astop`). It found no durable AGENTS.md update for it. The inline comment explains the change, and the change only applies to one handler.

title: Ignore Python 3.15 multi-threaded fork warning in forked child service test
body:
This PR fixes the `test_forked_child_exits_cleanly_with_running_service` failure on `main` for Python 3.15 ([failed run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40108528899)). #23464 added this test.

<details>

**Root cause**

The test starts a `MockService`, which starts a thread. Then the test calls `fork()`. Python 3.15 emits a `DeprecationWarning` ("This process ... is multi-threaded, use of fork() may lead to deadlocks in the child") when a multi-threaded process calls `fork()`. The pytest config sets `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]`, so the warning becomes an error. On Python 3.15 the test fails every time. It is not a random failure.

**Fix**

Add a `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` mark to ignore this warning for this test only. The test must fork while the service thread runs, so the warning is expected. This is the same mark that `test_manager_has_lock_information_when_deserialized_in_new_process_with_fork` in `tests/test_locking.py` uses (added in #23400).

**Verification**

- Python 3.15.1: the failure reproduces before the fix. After the fix, the test passes 20 of 20 runs, and `tests/_internal/concurrency/test_services.py` passes (48 tests).
- Default Python: `tests/_internal/concurrency/test_services.py` passes.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed file.

</details>

title: docs: document SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE rule in server AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds one Key Contracts bullet to `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`. The bullet says that SQLite transactions which read rows and then write based on them must pass `with_for_update=True` so SQLite starts with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. It also says the flag does nothing on PostgreSQL, where the locking `SELECT` needs `.with_for_update()`.

The same "database is locked" bug has now been fixed three separate times: #22967 and #23052 (`mark_deployments_ready`), and #23471 (automation buckets, the triggering push).

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**SQLite read-then-write transactions need `with_for_update=True`** — pass it to `session_context(begin_transaction=True, ...)` (or wrappers such as `automations_session`) when a transaction reads rows and then writes based on them, so SQLite starts with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. A default deferred transaction cannot upgrade to a write lock if another connection commits after its read, and fails immediately with "database is locked" under concurrent load (a recurring bug class). The flag is a no-op on PostgreSQL, so the locking `SELECT` also needs `.with_for_update()` there."
Non-obvious evidence: The session-level flag has the same name as SQLAlchemy's row-lock `.with_for_update()`, but it only changes SQLite's BEGIN mode (`SQLITE_BEGIN_MODE` in `database/configurations.py`). The PostgreSQL `begin_transaction` ignores it. The failure only appears under concurrent load, so you can't see it from the code or from single-connection tests. Three separate fixes (#22967, #23052, #23471) were needed for the same bug class.
Cross-cutting scope: Every server transaction that reads and then writes: API routes (`api/flow_runs.py`, `api/task_runs.py`), models (`models/deployments.py`), events (`events/triggers.py`) and services (`services/db_vacuum.py`).
Why not code comment/docstring: Comments exist at the call sites that were already fixed (`triggers.py`, `models/deployments.py`, `db_vacuum.py`). An agent writing a *new* transaction won't read those sites, and `session_context`'s docstring doesn't mention the flag. The rule is about how to write new code, not about any one function.
Durability: It depends on SQLite's deferred-transaction locking semantics and Prefect's dual-dialect support. Neither is tied to the triggering PR.
Counter-evidence checked: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md` (only says "SQLite and PostgreSQL must be kept in lockstep", with nothing on locking), `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, and every `AGENTS.md` in the repo (grepped for `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`with_for_update`: no matches). Also checked the `PrefectDBInterface.session_context` docstring, the `begin_transaction` implementations in `database/configurations.py`, and the `_maintenance_session` docstring in `db_vacuum.py`, which is the only other place the rule is stated, and only for that helper.

</details>

body:
This PR documents the SQLite read-then-write transaction contract in `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`. Passing `with_for_update=True` starts SQLite transactions with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, avoiding a stale deferred-read snapshot when another connection commits before the write. PostgreSQL ignores this session flag; query-level locking must be explicit there.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification and conflict resolution</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: Use `with_for_update=True` for SQLite transactions that read before writing, with explicit PostgreSQL query locking where required.
Non-obvious evidence: The session option changes SQLite transaction start behavior but does not add PostgreSQL row locks.
Cross-cutting scope: Server transaction callers across models, services and event processing.
Why not code comment/docstring: The configuration implementation already explains it, but callers across the server need this editing contract.
Durability: Applies to SQLite snapshot upgrades and the existing database session API.
Counter-evidence checked: SQLite and PostgreSQL `begin_transaction` implementations in `server/database/configurations.py`.

Merged main to resolve adjacent additions in this file. Retained both the original SQLite guidance and main's SQLAlchemy compatibility guidance unchanged; the PR difference from that main remains exactly the original one-line addition.

Validation: a disposable two-connection SQLite WAL reproduction confirmed deferred read followed by another connection's commit fails on write with `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`; an immediate read/write succeeds. Verified the resolved file equals main plus the original rule. Commit hooks passed. This is documentation-only; no server runtime code changed and the full database suite was not rerun.

this PR adds a short "Process-wide logging config" note to `tests/AGENTS.md`, next to the existing `PREFECT_HOME` cleanup pitfall: CLI invocations outside test mode (and uvicorn startup) reconfigure global logging, which leaks into later tests on the same xdist worker; restore with `setup_logging(incremental=False)` in fixture teardown.

Path: `tests/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: New "Process-wide logging config" subsection (1 paragraph) under Testing Guidelines: the CLI calls `setup_logging()` when not in test mode and uvicorn reconfigures logging on startup; tests that trigger either (e.g. `invoke_and_assert` under a fresh, non-test profile) replace process-wide logging config for later tests on the worker, surfacing as failures in unrelated tests asserting on DEBUG logs. title: Allow the provisioned ECS execution role to create CloudWatch log groups
body:
closes #20237

This PR lets the execution role created by `prefect work-pool create --type ecs:push --provision-infra` create CloudWatch log groups, and adds that permission to roles created by earlier versions when provisioning is run again.

`AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy` allows `logs:CreateLogStream` and `logs:PutLogEvents` but not `logs:CreateLogGroup`. The ECS worker sets `awslogs-create-group: "true"` when `configure_cloudwatch_logs` is enabled, so tasks failed to start with the `AccessDeniedException` in the issue.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `ExecutionRoleResource` now puts an inline role policy, `PrefectEcsTaskExecutionRoleLogsPolicy`, that allows only `logs:CreateLogGroup`. The other two log actions already come from the AWS managed policy, so they are not repeated.
- Whether the role needs the policy is checked separately from whether the role exists (`get_role_policy`). This covers the upgrade path @desertaxle raised on #21805: an existing role without the policy now shows up in the planned actions and the task count, and gets the policy on the next run. A role that already has it is left alone.
- An inline policy keeps the change scoped to the role and makes the re-run idempotent (`put_role_policy` overwrites by name), so no extra customer-managed policy has to be looked up across pages of `list_policies`.
- `Resource` is `*` because the log group name can be overridden through `cloudwatch_logs_options`; the default is `prefect`.
- The docs list of IAM permissions needed to run the provisioner gains `iam:GetRolePolicy` and `iam:PutRolePolicy`.

Tests in `tests/infrastructure/provisioners/test_ecs.py` (moto):

- a new role gets `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy` plus the logs policy, with the exact statement asserted
- an existing role without the logs policy (new `existing_execution_role_without_logs_policy` fixture) requires provisioning, lists one planned action, counts one task, and gets the policy on `provision()`
- `existing_execution_role` now represents a fully provisioned role, so the "nothing to do" cases still assert no work
- task counts and planned actions for `AuthenticationResource` updated for the extra step

`uv run pytest tests/infrastructure/provisioners/test_ecs.py`: 85 passed. Without the source change, 10 of the 19 `TestExecutionRoleResource` and `TestAuthenticationResource` tests fail. `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

Reproduced with moto before the change: the provisioned role's policies allow `logs:CreateLogStream` and `logs:PutLogEvents` only, and a second provisioning run does not change that. After the change, both runs end with `logs:CreateLogGroup` allowed.

</details>

title: Fix flaky `StateFilter` discovery cap search test
body:
This PR fixes the flaky `searches beyond the discovery cap and keeps deleted selected names` test in `state-filter.test.tsx`. It failed on `main` in [UI v2 Checks run 40103970615](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40103970615) (commit 213a369488c4983e8c4e7256b6eb4b62ac5540d4) with `Unable to find role="menuitem" and name "Baseline, NOT Met"`.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

`useStateOptions` debounces the search query by 300ms before it sends the `/observed-states?query=Base` request. The test types "Base" and then calls `findByRole`, which waits 1000ms by default. The 300ms debounce, the MSW response, and the re-render all had to finish inside that 1000ms. Instrumented local runs showed that the time from the end of typing to the request was 300–510ms under load. On a busy CI runner, the full sequence can go above 1000ms.

The fix uses `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` in this test, with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers })`. The test then calls `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300)` after it types. This advances the debounce on purpose, so the debounce does not use the `findByRole` wait time. `afterEach` restores real timers. This is the same pattern as `rich-date-range-selector.test.tsx`.

Verification:
- Before the fix, the test failed 1 of 3 times when run alone on its own.
- After the fix, it passed 24 of 24 runs (3 rounds of 8 parallel runs on 8 cores). The full file passes.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run check` pass.

</details>

body:
this PR expands the `test-projects/` entry in `tests/AGENTS.md`: the directory is shared, mutable state under xdist (other tests import/execute its modules and write `__pycache__`), so tests that write to a project or assert on its directory contents should copy it into `tmp_path` first. This matches the existing `project_dir` fixtures in `tests/cli/test_deploy.py`, `tests/deployment/test_base.py`, `tests/experimental/test_sla.py`, and the new `tree_project` fixture from #23554.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `tests/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: Extend the `test-projects/` bullet with: "Treat as read-only shared state: under xdist, other tests import and execute modules in these directories (writing `__pycache__`), so copy into `tmp_path` (`shutil.copytree`) before writing to a project or asserting on its directory contents"
Non-obvious evidence: The failure only shows up when an unrelated test on another xdist worker imports a module from the same project mid-test (#23554 flake on `TestRemoteFileSystem` tree-project tests). Nothing at the `test-projects/` directory or in `tests/AGENTS.md` says the directory is mutated at runtime; the only explanation is a local comment on one fixture in `tests/test_filesystems.py`.
Cross-cutting scope: Applies to every test that uses `TEST_PROJECTS_DIR` (defined independently in ~10 test modules across `tests/cli/`, `tests/deployment/`, `tests/experimental/`, `tests/utilities/`, `tests/test_filesystems.py`), not one helper.
Why not code comment/docstring: `TEST_PROJECTS_DIR` is redefined per module with no shared definition to attach a comment to; an author writing a new test elsewhere will not see the comment in `test_filesystems.py`.
Durability: Holds as long as tests run under xdist and import modules from `test-projects/` — independent of the triggering PR.
Counter-evidence checked: `tests/AGENTS.md` (only a one-line description of `test-projects/`), `tests/fixtures/AGENTS.md` (no mention), root `AGENTS.md`, `tests/conftest.py` (no shared `TEST_PROJECTS_DIR` fixture), existing `project_dir` fixtures (already follow the copy pattern without explaining why).

title: Fix flaky `TestRemoteFileSystem` tree-project tests
body:
This PR fixes the flaky test `tests/test_filesystems.py::TestRemoteFileSystem::test_put_directory_put_file_count` (failed on `main` in [run 40024246163](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40024246163) with `assert 5 == 6`).

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

**Root cause:** The test reads `tests/test-projects/tree-project` directly. This directory is shared. Tests in `tests/utilities/test_importtools.py` import modules from `tree-project`. These imports write `__pycache__` entries into the directory. Under xdist, the two test files run at the same time on different workers (both ran in group 14 of the failed run).

`filter_files` walks the tree two times: one walk for `ignored_files`, one walk for `all_files`. If a `__pycache__/*.pyc` file appears between the two walks, the file is not in `ignored_files` but it is in `all_files`. Thus it is counted as included. `put_directory` does its own walks. The two counts in the test then can be different.

**Fix:** Add a `tree_project` fixture that copies `tree-project` (without `__pycache__`) into `tmp_path`. `test_put_directory_put_file_count` and `test_put_directory_tree` now use this private copy, so other workers cannot change the directory during the test.

**Verification:**
- Reproduced locally with a background script that creates and removes `tree-project/imports/__pycache__/*.pyc` in a loop: the original test failed with the same count mismatch.
- With the fix and the same background script: 25/25 runs passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_filesystems.py tests/utilities/test_importtools.py -n auto --maxprocesses 6`: 125 passed, 1 skipped.
</details>

title: docs: document Rich markup/emoji pitfall for CLI JSON output
body:
This PR adds one rule to `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`: print JSON and other verbatim user data with `markup=False, emoji=False`.

Rich `console.print` reads `[...]` as markup and `:name:` as emoji aliases. This silently changes JSON payloads, or raises `MarkupError` on a stray closing tag. #23530 fixed this for `prefect variable`, but many other `--output json` paths in `src/prefect/cli/` still call `_cli.console.print(json_output, soft_wrap=True)` without these flags. The rule tells future agents about the hazard before they add or change JSON output.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**Print JSON and other verbatim user data with `markup=False, emoji=False`.** `console.print` otherwise parses `[...]` as Rich markup and `:name:` as emoji aliases, silently rewriting payloads (or raising `MarkupError` on stray closing tags). `print_json` and `Pretty` are not affected."
Non-obvious evidence: The shared console (`_app.py`) sets `highlight=False` but keeps Rich's markup and emoji parsing on. Corruption only occurs when user data contains brackets or `:alias:` text, so normal tests do not find it. Before #23530 no CLI code passed `markup=False`. Verified locally: `console.print('{"a": "[bold]x[/bold] :smile:"}')` outputs `{"a": "x 😄"}`, and `'[/red]'` raises `MarkupError`. `print_json(data=...)` and `Pretty(...)` keep the text unchanged.
Cross-cutting scope: All CLI command groups that emit JSON or echo user values through `_cli.console.print` (for example `deployment`, `flow_run`, `task_run`, `work_queue`, `artifact`, `concurrency_limit`, `global_concurrency_limit`, `profile`, `config`, `cloud`). This is not specific to `variable.py`.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to each new output call in every command module. No single function owns it, so a comment in one place does not reach agents who edit other modules. The CLI AGENTS.md already holds the JSON-output contract next to this rule.
Durability: Rich defaults will not change, and new `--output json` commands are added often. The rule stays useful after #23530 is old.
Counter-evidence checked: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md` (the JSON bullet covers mixing stray prints only), root `AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`, and `tests/AGENTS.md` (no mention of markup/emoji). `_app.py` console setup (no `markup=False`). `variable.py` has no explaining comment. `tests/cli/test_variable.py` covers only the variable commands.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in triggering push (6b8f5e6581..96b160acb0)</summary>

- `src/prefect/cli/variable.py`
- `tests/cli/test_variable.py`

</details>
