title: Bump lodash-es and mermaid in /ui-v2
body:
Bumps [lodash-es](https://github.com/lodash/lodash) to 4.18.1 and updates ancestor dependency [mermaid](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `lodash-es` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash-es's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend
  • lodash.sortedindexby
  • lodash.zipobjectdeep
  • lodash.unset
  • lodash.omit
  • lodash.template

title: Stabilize CLI startup benchmark regression checks
body:
This PR changes the CLI startup benchmark gate so that runner timing drift does not cause false regression failures. A repeatable slowdown greater than 15% still fails the gate.

<details>
<summary>Problem</summary>

The `CLI startup benchmarks` check fails on PRs that do not change CLI startup, and the same commit passes on rerun. Example: [run 39992885993, job 120548906391](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39992885993/job/120548906391) reported `prefect deployment --help` at +23.7% with p=0.0029. The [rerun](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39992885993/job/120586251318) measured +7.0% and passed. Other recovered failures: [39996026421](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39996026421/job/120559705783), [39305085922](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39305085922/job/118239993139).

The causes:

1. The job ran the full base suite, then the full head suite. Runner slowdown during the head batch looked like a head regression.
2. SciPy was not installed, so `cli-bench compare` used a normal approximation. With 5 samples, this gives p-values that are too small. The correct Welch p-value for the example is approximately 0.039.
3. Each of the 28 commands used p < 0.05 alone, with no correction for the number of commands.
4. The metadata in `baseline.json` and `comparison.json` recorded the merge checkout SHA, not the measured revisions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Approach</summary>

The new helper `scripts/cli_startup_benchmark.py` replaces the `cli-bench run`/`cli-bench compare` steps for each shard:

- For each command, it runs warmups, then 10 rounds. Each round runs base and head back to back. The order alternates (base→head, head→base), so drift affects both revisions equally.
- The decision uses the paired log ratio `ln(head/base)` for each round. The effect is the geometric-mean change. Significance uses a one-sided paired t-test (`scipy.stats.ttest_1samp`, from the existing `python-cli-bench[stats]` extra).
- A command is a `regression` when the effect is more than 15% and p < 0.05 / 28 (Bonferroni over all commands in all shards, not per shard).
- A large effect that is not significant is `inconclusive`. It is shown in the summary but does not fail the job.
- Command failures, timeouts, invalid timings, and fewer than 6 complete pairs give `error` and fail the job. Partial artifacts are still written.
- The helper checks that each worktree is at the requested SHA, and records the SHA and `prefect --version` of each target.
- It runs each target's `.venv/bin` executable directly. The workflow runs `uv sync --locked --no-dev` in each worktree before measurement, so `uv run` resolution is not timed.

The four shards, `fail-fast: false`, the `CLI startup benchmarks` aggregate job, and the artifact file names (`baseline.json`, `comparison.json`, `cli-benchmark-compare.md`, `cli-benchmark-digest.json`) do not change. The digest now also includes raw paired samples and decision parameters. Changes to the helper or its tests trigger the benchmark workflow, and shard 0 runs the helper tests.

Tradeoffs:

- Each shard runs about 2 × (2 + 10) invocations per command, against 2 × 5 (plus hyperfine warmups) before. Shard runtime increases.
- With the Bonferroni correction, a small slowdown just above 15% can be `inconclusive` instead of a failure when the runner is noisy. A stable slowdown greater than 15% still fails.
- The helper is approximately 540 lines, more than a minimal script, because it also writes the existing artifact formats and verifies target identity.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- `tests/scripts/test_cli_startup_benchmark.py` (24 tests, no wall-clock dependency): alternating order and target identity; synthetic shared drift does not fail; a stable +20% slowdown under drift fails; the captured 5-sample case is not an unqualified regression; full-family correction; fail-closed errors with partial artifacts; a smoke test with two temporary git targets.
- A local one-command comparison of `prefect --version` between `origin/main~1` and `origin/main` gave +0.1%, `ok`, and wrote all four artifacts. This does not show a change in the CI flake rate. Only CI runs over time can show that.

</details>

title: docs: document flow archival and restoration policies
body:
Refs [CLOUD-4655](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/CLOUD-4655/document-flow-archival).

This PR documents flow archival in Prefect Cloud so customers can retire flows without deleting run history and restore them when needed. It adds a guide for manual and bulk archival, the two workspace policies, API filtering, and older-client compatibility; updates the flows and automations concepts; and documents the three archival events and the archived-flow label on flow-run events.

The guide describes the current UI: the All and Favorites tabs with a menu for the Unarchived, All, and Archived views, **Pause and archive** for flows with schedules that are on, the warning for deployments that automations run, and the run block for archived flows while the Archived flow restoration policy is off.

<details>
<summary>Behavior and validation</summary>

The documentation follows the current nebula and nebula-ui implementation and the Prefect voice guide. Both policies are documented as off by default. The guide explains deployment schedule requirements, retention-limited inactivity windows, the dormant flow eligibility rules, gradual archival, and restoration when matching run events arrive.

The guide says archiving deletes a flow's scheduled runs that haven't started. That behavior is in a Prefect Cloud change that hasn't shipped yet, so this PR waits for it.

Validation:
- `mint broken-links` passed.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed.
- JSON examples, navigation entries, new internal links, and Mintlify-generated anchors checked.

Keep this PR in draft until the feature rollout is ready for customer-facing documentation.
</details>

title: Document OIDC identity tokens for Modal push work pools
body:
This PR adds one paragraph and an example to the Modal tab of the serverless push work pool guide (`docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/serverless.mdx`).

<details>

The paragraph explains the new **Include OIDC Identity Token** work pool toggle. When it is on, Modal injects `MODAL_IDENTITY_TOKEN` into each sandbox. The paragraph links to [Modal's OIDC integration guide](https://modal.com/docs/guide/oidc-integration) for the AWS trust setup. It shows the `AWS_ROLE_ARN` + `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` pattern: write the token to a file, then let boto3 assume the role and re-assume it when the credentials expire. Runs that last longer than the role's maximum session duration continue to work.

The example uses `{/* pmd-metadata: notest */}` because it needs Modal and AWS credentials.

The Prefect Cloud change that adds the toggle is tracked in the internal ticket CLOUD-5439.

</details>

title: Bump graphql-core from 3.2.7 to 3.2.12
body:
Bumps [graphql-core](https://github.com/graphql-python/graphql-core) from 3.2.7 to 3.2.12.
Release notes

Sourced from graphql-core's releases.

v3.2.12

Patch-release GraphQL-core v3.2.12, based on GraphQL.js v16.14.2.

This patch-release supports Python 3.7 to 3.14.

This is a security release. It fixes two denial-of-service vulnerabilities in the validator and the parser. Upgrading is recommended for all users.

Security fixes:

  • CVE-2026-75507 (GHSA-vj8h-fx38-h3vc, High) — the OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged validation rule could be driven into quadratic and worse running time by a small, highly compressible query using repeated inline fragments, occupying a worker for minutes of CPU during validation, before any resolver runs. Validation now enforces a per-document comparison budget and aborts with a GraphQLError once it is exhausted.
  • CVE-2026-75508 (GHSA-r77w-qph3-7vf8, High) — comment tokens were allocated and retained but not counted toward the parser's max_tokens limit, so a comment-padded document could bypass the limit while allocating one token object per comment. max_tokens now counts every token the parser consumes, including skipped comments.

Please note the two behaviour changes this implies:

  • A pathological query that previously validated — slowly — now produces a validation error. Realistic queries stay far below the limit, which defaults to 250,000 field comparisons and can be adjusted by assigning to graphql.validation.rules.overlapping_fields_can_be_merged.MAX_FIELD_COMPARISONS.
  • Comments now count toward max_tokens, so a comment-heavy document that was previously accepted may now be rejected. If you parse documents with substantial comments and set max_tokens, you may need to raise the limit. The token_count of a parsed document now includes comments as well.

Both limits complement, but do not replace, a request body-size limit applied to the decompressed request body in your web framework.

Other changes:

  • Updated development dependencies and CI tooling.

The security issues were reported by @​BZHunt, who also reviewed the fixes before release. In memory of ZaX, who was the driving force behind this discovery. The first one was also independently found and diagnosed by @​bcmyguest.

Thanks to @​jkimbo for sponsoring this project.

This patch-release supports Python 3.7 to 3.14.

Notable changes:

  • Add support for directives on directive definitions
  • Restore variable own-property checks in value_from_ast
  • Remove unused variable-definition tracking in ValuesOfCorrectTypeRule

title: Bump virtualenv from 21.7.13 to 21.14.9
body:
Bumps [virtualenv](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv) from 21.7.13 to 21.14.9.
Release notes

Sourced from virtualenv's releases.

21.14.9

Bugfixes - 21.14.9

  • Parse VIRTUALENV_PERIODIC_UPDATE_INSECURE as a boolean, so 0, false, no and off keep certificate verification enabled. (#3398)

  • Reject destinations whose resolved path contains the platform's PATH separator, including separators inherited from the working directory or a directory symlink. (#3399)

  • Preserve an existing pyvenv.cfg when a prompt or configuration value cannot be encoded as UTF-8, instead of leaving the file empty after a failed environment creation. The file now ends its lines with LF on every platform.

    Debug logs show each configuration line as a Python string literal, so control characters are visible. (#3400)

  • Skip writing a .venv redirect when the environment name contains a line boundary. The environment is still created, and any existing redirect remains unchanged. (#3401)

  • Preserve non-ASCII values in activate_this.py when applications read the script with a legacy text encoding before executing it. (#3402)

  • Reject malformed seed versions and requirements ending in archive suffixes before starting pip, with an error identifying the invalid value instead of a misleading download or local-file error. (#3403)

  • Allow a literal percent sign as a csh prompt and preserve carets in tcsh prompt display instead of interpreting them as control-character notation.

    Separate csh history and prompt escapes from preceding non-ASCII text in legacy locales. (#3404)

  • Report an error when an existing pyvenv.cfg is not a regular file, instead of trying to read or write directories, pipes, or devices as configuration files. (#3405)

  • Preserve percent-containing paths during batch reactivation and show dollar signs literally in command prompts. Skip batch scripts for paths containing line boundaries, and remove stale batch scripts for unsupported paths even when only other activators are selected. (#3406)

  • Compile shared seed-cache bytecode without loading site customizations from the destination environment or importing modules from the current working directory. (#3407)

  • Keep the bundled seed version when a cached periodic update is older, and stop recording downloads below the bundled version during update checks. (#3408)

  • Stop activating a moved environment, leaving PATH unchanged, when the shell is not bash, the script is evaluated or read from standard input, a path tool fails, the sourced file is not the environment's own activation script, or the new location has no pyvenv.cfg, instead of continuing with an incorrect environment path. (#3409)

  • Reject built-in options with missing values before creating the application-data directory or starting interpreter discovery, instead of reporting the argument error after those operations. (#3410)

  • Keep unset-variable bookkeeping out of exported xonsh variables, so child shells do not restore an internal sentinel as PYTHONHOME. Skip xonsh activation for destination names that its PATH handling would expand to a different path.

    Restore unset Tcl/Tk library variables when switching between environments in one xonsh session.

    Preserve non-ASCII paths and prompts when xonsh reads activation scripts with a legacy encoding. (#3411)

  • Skip default shell activators with a warning when a POSIX path encoding is incompatible with their UTF-8 scripts. Explicitly requested incompatible shell activators still report an error. Environments created with --activators= or --activators=python remain supported in legacy locales. Undecodable parent paths are now caught before any shell activation script is written. (#3412)

title: docs: document whenever 0.11 compat rules in prefect AGENTS.md
body:
This PR updates the `whenever` compat bullet in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` for whenever 0.11 (now allowed by #23164).

The bullet now says:
- Compat flags use feature detection, not version checks: `_WHENEVER_NEW_API` (>= 0.10.0) and `_SYSTEM_TZ` (>= 0.11).
- Do not call `.assume_system_tz()` / `.to_system_tz()` directly. They are deprecated in 0.11, and the deprecation warning fails tests because pytest uses `filterwarnings = error`. Use `in_local_tz()`.
- Do not import `DateTimeDelta` directly. It is removed in 0.11. Use the `Interval` alias.

The edit changes one line in place (net 0 lines).

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: Replace "abstract over API differences between whenever 0.7.x–0.9.x and ≥ 0.10.0. The `_WHENEVER_NEW_API` flag ... guards version-specific code." with a statement that the helpers cover supported whenever releases through feature-detection flags (`_WHENEVER_NEW_API`, `_SYSTEM_TZ`). Add `.assume_system_tz()`/`.to_system_tz()` (use `in_local_tz()`) and direct `DateTimeDelta` imports (use `Interval`) to the existing list of forbidden direct whenever calls.
Non-obvious evidence: The only note about the 0.11 change is one inline comment in `types/_datetime.py`. Code outside that module cannot see it. I confirmed on whenever 0.11.0 that `assume_system_tz()` and `to_system_tz()` emit `WheneverDeprecationWarning`. `pyproject.toml` sets `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]`, so a new direct call fails tests on Python 3.13+ only. `whenever.DateTimeDelta` does not exist in 0.11.0.
Cross-cutting scope: All Python 3.13+ datetime code in `src/prefect/` (client and server). For example, `server/schemas/schedules.py` needed a matching `DateTimeDelta` fix in the same push.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule is about code written outside `types/_datetime.py`. Contributors read the AGENTS.md bullet before they write new datetime code. They do not read a comment inside the helper module first.
Durability: The repo supports a range of whenever versions (`>=0.10.5,<0.12.0`), so the feature-detection pattern and these forbidden calls stay relevant until the lower bound moves past 0.11.
Counter-evidence checked: The existing `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` whenever bullet (it was stale: it named only 0.7–0.10 differences). `tests/fixtures/AGENTS.md` (only pendulum/`frozen_time` guidance). The inline comments and `in_local_tz()` in `types/_datetime.py`. The `schedules.py` fallback. No other AGENTS.md mentions whenever 0.11, `SYSTEM_TZ`, or `DateTimeDelta`.
</details>

<details>

- `client/pyproject.toml`
- `pyproject.toml`

title: Lock current prefect-redis and prefect-kubernetes for the Docker image
body:
closes #23536

This PR updates `uv.lock` to prefect-redis 0.3.0 and prefect-kubernetes 0.8.0, which the Docker image installs since #23225. It also fixes the reason the lock fell behind.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

### Root cause

Dependency bots clone without tags (see the existing comment in `pyproject.toml`). In those clones versioningit uses `default-tag`, so the local `prefect` resolves as `3.6.24+...`. Newer integration releases need a newer `prefect`:

| Package | Last release `uv lock` can pick at 3.6.24 | First release it can't pick | Floor of that release |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| prefect-redis | 0.2.11 | 0.2.12 | `prefect>=3.7.4` |
| prefect-kubernetes | 0.7.x | 0.7.13 | `prefect>=3.8.4` |

So every lock update from those clones kept, or moved the lock back to, these old releases. Reproduced in a `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` checkout: `uv lock --upgrade-package prefect-kubernetes --upgrade-package prefect-redis` moved the lock *down* to 0.7.7 / 0.2.11 (resolver output: `prefect-kubernetes >0.7.13 depends on prefect >=3.8.4`).

### Changes

- `pyproject.toml`: raise versioningit `default-version` / `default-tag` from 3.6.24 to 3.9.0. That is at or above the highest in-repo integration floor, which is now `prefect>=3.8.4`.
- `uv.lock`: `uv lock --upgrade-package prefect-redis --upgrade-package prefect-kubernetes`. Only these two entries change.
- `tests/_internal/test_integrations.py`: new test that both fallback versions satisfy the `prefect` requirement of every `src/integrations/*/pyproject.toml`. It fails on `main` (`3.6.24+nogit` does not satisfy `prefect>=3.8.4` from prefect-aws). So the next time an integration raises its floor, the test will flag that the fallback needs raising too.

### Verification

- In the tagless clone with this branch: `uv lock --check` passes, and re-running the upgrade keeps 0.8.0 / 0.3.0. Before this change it downgraded them.
- Installed `.[redis,kubernetes,client,otel]` with `--constraint` from `uv export --frozen --no-dev --all-extras --no-emit-project --no-hashes`, the same command the Dockerfile runs. Result: prefect-redis 0.3.0 and prefect-kubernetes 0.8.0, and `import prefect_redis.cleanup_queue` works.
- Did not run a full `docker build` locally. The existing `uv sync --check` step in `run-docker-tests` checks that the image matches the lock.

### Not changed

Other integrations are also behind their latest releases in the lock, for example prefect-aws 0.7.7 vs 0.7.12 and prefect-gcp 0.6.17 vs 0.6.22. The published image flavors don't install them, so this PR leaves them alone. Now that the fallback is fixed, a normal lock refresh can update them.

</details>

title: Retry flows that return a failed state when `retries` is configured
body:
closes #23534

This PR makes flow-level `retries` work when a flow *returns* a state (or futures/states) that resolve to `Failed`, instead of raising.

<details>

Before, `RetryFailedFlows` on the server turned the proposed `Failed` into `AwaitingRetry` and set `retry_type="in_process"`. `handle_exception` and `handle_timeout` catch this case and go back to `Running`. `handle_success` (sync and async) did not, so the engine loop exited. The run was left in `AwaitingRetry`, and workers skip `in_process` runs, so nothing ever picked it up.

`handle_success` now does the same check in both engines, but only when the proposed terminal state was failed (`terminal_state.is_failed() and state.is_scheduled()`). In that case it logs, resets `_return_value` to `NotSet`, sets `Running`, and returns early, which skips the success telemetry and the result linking. Resetting `_return_value` matters: `run_context` re-raises exceptions whenever `_return_value` is set, so without the reset, an exception on the retry attempt would skip `handle_exception`. When a flow explicitly returns `Scheduled()` or `AwaitingRetry()`, that state is kept and the body is not re-run.

Tests in `TestFlowRetries` cover:
- sync and async flows that return `Failed` every time (body runs twice, ends `Failed`)
- sync and async flows that return `Failed` first and then succeed
- a flow that returns `Failed` first and then raises
- a flow that returns a submitted task future whose task fails on the first attempt
- sync and async flows that return `Scheduled`/`AwaitingRetry`, with `retries=0` and `retries=1` (state is kept, body runs once)

Reproduced with the script from the issue: before, `body runs=1 SCHEDULED/AwaitingRetry retry_type='in_process'`; after, `body runs=2 FAILED/Failed retry_type=None`.

</details>

title: Read `.env` once per process when loading settings
body:
closes #23532

This PR makes `import prefect` open `./.env` one time instead of 216 times (FIFO) or 324 times (regular file). This stops the startup stall when `.env` is a 1Password Environments mount (a FIFO).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The issue says all reads come from `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource`. Measurement shows three sources of reads per settings class load (54 classes, 2 loads each during import):

| Caller | Opens (before) |
|---|---|
| pydantic-settings default `DotEnvSettingsSource` (built in `BaseSettings._settings_init_sources`, then discarded by `PrefectBaseSettings.settings_customise_sources`) | 108 |
| `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource` | 108 |
| `_get_profiles_path` (regular files only) | 108 |

Changes:

- `src/prefect/settings/sources.py`: add `_read_dotenv_file`. It caches the raw `.env` contents in the existing `_file_cache` TTL cache (the same cache as `_read_toml_file`, cleared with `_file_cache.clear()`). Each call parses the cached contents with `dotenv.dotenv_values(stream=...)`, so `${VAR}` interpolation uses the current environment.
  - Regular files: the cache key includes inode, size and `st_mtime_ns`, so a changed `.env` is read again.
  - FIFOs: the cache key does not include `stat` data, so the file is read again after the TTL (60 s).
  - `_dotenv_file_lock` serializes loads, so concurrent cache misses open the file once.
  - `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource._read_env_file` and `_get_profiles_path` use this function.
- `src/prefect/settings/base.py`: `build_settings_config` now sets `env_file` to `_DEFAULT_ENV_FILE`, an empty `_DefaultEnvFile` tuple. The default pydantic-settings dotenv source therefore has no file to read, and `PrefectBaseSettings.settings_customise_sources` passes `.env` to `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource` in its place. Any other `env_file` value set by a subclass (a path, or `None` to not load a dotenv file) is passed through unchanged, as before.

Result with `repros/23532.py` (the issue's script):

```
before: .env opened 216 times during `import prefect`   (FIFO)
        .env opened 324 times during `import prefect`   (regular file)
after:  .env opened 1 times during `import prefect`     (FIFO and regular file)
```

Also checked with pydantic-settings 2.9.1 (lowest supported), 2.14.2 (locked) and 2.16.1.

Tests (in `TestSettingsSources`):
- `test_dotenv_file_read_once_across_settings_sources`
- `test_dotenv_file_changes_are_reloaded`
- `test_dotenv_fifo_read_once_across_settings_sources` (a thread serves the FIFO; skipped on pydantic-settings < 2.14, which does not read FIFOs)
- `test_dotenv_file_read_once_by_concurrent_settings_loads`
- `test_dotenv_file_interpolation_uses_current_environment`
- `test_env_file_can_be_overridden` (custom path, and the `env_file=None` opt-out)

`tests/test_settings.py`, `tests/cli/test_config.py` and `tests/cli/test_profile.py` pass.

</details>

title: Cache `get_timezones()`
body:
Cache `get_timezones()` so schedule validation stops rescanning tzdata.

`get_timezones()` calls `zoneinfo.available_timezones()`, which walks the tzdata files on disk (~2.5 ms) on every call. It runs whenever a schedule with a `timezone` is validated, which includes every schedule the server reads from the database. Validation is synchronous, so these scans block the event loop in the scheduler service and in worker deployment reads.

The function returns an immutable tuple, so this PR adds `@cache`.

### Impact

```python
import time
from prefect.client.schemas.schedules import CronSchedule

N = 1000
start = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(N):
    CronSchedule(cron="*/5 * * * *", timezone="America/New_York")
print(f"{(time.perf_counter() - start) / N * 1000:.3f} ms per validation")
```

| | Per validation | Scheduler pass, 500 deployments |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 2.56 ms | 7.0 s (3.9 s in `get_timezones`) |
| After | 0.04 ms | 2.7 s |

**Tradeoff:** tzdata is read once per process, so a tzdata update made while a process is running won't be picked up until it restarts. This matches prefect.types.TimeZone, which already builds its list once at import.

### Tests

Added `test_get_timezones_scans_tzdata_once`: validating two schedules calls `available_timezones()` exactly once.

title: Preserve literal markup and emoji aliases in variable CLI JSON output
body:
closes #23529

This PR stops Rich from changing variable values in machine-readable output. `prefect variable get`, `prefect variable inspect --output json`, and `prefect variable ls --output json` now print serialized JSON with `markup=False` and `emoji=False`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Before this change, Rich parsed the JSON text as markup. A value such as `[red]literal[/red]` became `literal`, and `:smile:` became an emoji. A value such as `literal [/unexpected]` caused `rich.errors.MarkupError`.
- `variable get` now also uses `soft_wrap=True`, so long values do not get line breaks at the terminal width when `PREFECT_CLI_WRAP_LINES` is enabled. The two `--output json` paths already used it.
- Human-readable output (the `ls` table and the `inspect` pretty view) and the global console do not change.

The tests run with `PREFECT_CLI_WRAP_LINES=True` and give the variable literal markup/emoji tags, which `inspect` and `ls` JSON must also keep. All 15 new cases fail on `main` and pass with this change.

Other CLI commands use the same `console.print(json_output, soft_wrap=True)` pattern. This PR does not change them, to keep the scope to the reported issue.

</details>

title: Bump stale integration pins in uv.lock and keep them current on release
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23524
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23536

this PR:
- bumps every `prefect-*` pin in `uv.lock` that was behind PyPI — kubernetes 0.7.6→0.8.0, redis 0.2.11→0.3.0, aws 0.7.7→0.7.12, azure 0.4.8→0.4.13, bitbucket 0.3.6→0.3.7, docker 0.7.1→0.7.4, email 0.4.2→0.4.3, gcp 0.6.17→0.6.22, github 0.4.2→0.4.4, gitlab 0.3.4→0.3.5, ray 0.5.0→0.6.0, shell 0.3.6→0.3.7, slack 0.3.1→0.4.0, snowflake 0.28.8→0.28.9
- adds a workflow that keeps `uv.lock` integration pins current going forward, via a release-tag-triggered bump plus a weekly sweep

<details>

Since the Dockerfile installs extras via `uv pip install --constraint /dist/constraints.txt` (generated from `uv export --frozen --all-extras`), the images ship whatever version of each integration `uv.lock` pins — and every integration pin constrains every image flavor. The lock held stale pins since 3.6.24: kubernetes 0.7.6 (3.8.1 images shipped 0.7.11, missing the observer fix from #22965 released in 0.7.13) and redis 0.2.11 (3.8.7 images shipped 0.2.15, missing `prefect_redis.cleanup_queue` added in 0.2.12), so upgrading images downgraded bundled integrations.

Bumps generated with `uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg>` for each stale pin. Verified `uv export --frozen --no-dev --all-extras` now constrains `prefect-kubernetes==0.8.0` and `prefect-redis==0.3.0`. The only non-integration lock change is setuptools 83.0.0→80.10.2, required by prefect-azure 0.4.13's `setuptools<81` constraint.

The new workflow (`.github/workflows/update-uv-lock-integrations.yaml`) keeps pins current two ways:
- **Tag push** — fires on the same `prefect-<name>-<semver>` tag pushes as `integration-package-release.yaml`, runs `uv lock --upgrade-package <released package>` on main, and opens a PR. No-ops for tags whose package isn't in the lock, when the pin is already current, or when a bump branch exists.
- **Weekly sweep** (Mondays 15:00 UTC, also `workflow_dispatch`) — upgrades every `prefect-*` pin behind PyPI and opens one PR, as a backstop for releases cut before the tag-triggered path existed or any bump PR that was missed.

</details>

title: Fix `KubernetesJobRun.wait_for_completion` raising on interim K8s 1.31+ Job conditions
body:
closes #23525

This PR makes `KubernetesJobRun.await_for_completion` treat only `Complete=True` (success) and `Failed=True` (failure) as terminal. Before this, any `True` condition other than `Complete` counted as a failure. On Kubernetes 1.31+ a Job can first show `SuccessCriteriaMet` or `FailureTarget` before its terminal condition is set, and in that window the method raised `RuntimeError: Job '...' failed due to []`, even for jobs that went on to succeed.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The loop now works out which condition types are `True` once per poll. It reuses that set for the existing `job_is_terminal` log-capture check and for the completion branch.
- When no terminal condition is present, the loop sleeps for `interval_seconds` and counts that time toward `timeout_seconds`. This also covers jobs with `active=0` and no conditions, where the old loop polled again immediately with no sleep.
- Added tests for `SuccessCriteriaMet` followed by `Complete`, which now succeeds, and `FailureTarget` followed by `Failed`, which now raises with the real reason. Both tests fail without this change.

</details>

Returning `Failed` state caches the exception and later calls skip execution.

Check this example:

```python
from uuid import uuid4

from prefect import task
from prefect.cache_policies import INPUTS
from prefect.states import Failed

attempts = 0

@task(cache_policy=INPUTS)
def charge_customer(order_id: str):
    global attempts
    attempts += 1

    if attempts == 1:
        return Failed(data=ValueError("Payment API temporarily unavailable"))

    return {"order_id": order_id, "status": "paid"}

order_id = str(uuid4())

first = charge_customer(order_id, return_state=True)
print(first.name, first.type.value, attempts)
# Failed FAILED 1

second = charge_customer(order_id, return_state=True)
print(second.name, second.type.value, attempts)
# Cached COMPLETED 1

print(repr(second.result()))  # Returns normally; does not raise.
# ValueError('Payment API temporarily unavailable')
```

Fixed by excluding peristed failures from sync and async tasks.

title: fix(cli/automation): delete every automation with prefect automation delete --all
body:
closes #23504

### Summary

This PR fixes `prefect automation delete --all` so that it pages through all automations rather than reading only the first page returned by `client.read_automations()` (which defaults to `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, 200 rows). It mirrors the fix applied to `prefect deployment delete --all` in #23440.

### Root Cause & Changes

- **Accurate total count for confirmation**: Pages `client.read_automations(offset=total)` until an empty page is returned, summing page lengths to report the true count before prompting the user.
- **Safe repeated deletion**: Repeatedly reads and deletes from the start of the list until no automations remain. Reading from offset 0 ensures the result set continuously shrinks without being affected by sorting instability across page boundaries.
- **Verification**: Added `test_deleting_all_automations_across_pages` in `tests/events/client/cli/test_automations.py` to verify multi-page pagination and deletion count.

title: Delete every automation with `prefect automation delete --all`
body:
closes #23504

this PR fixes `prefect automation delete --all` so that it deletes every automation instead of only the automations returned by the first page of results.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

### The problem

`prefect automation delete --all` called `read_automations()` once and deleted whatever that single call returned. The API returns at most `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT` (200 by default) automations per request, so any installation with more automations than that silently left the remainder behind — while still reporting that everything had been deleted:

```
$ prefect automation delete --all
? Are you sure you want to delete all 200 automations? [y/n] (n): y
Deleted 200 automations.
```

With 201 automations, one was left behind and the summary said `Deleted 200 automations.`

This is the same bug that #23440 fixed for `prefect deployment delete --all`; this PR applies the same approach to automations.

### The fix

`src/prefect/cli/automation.py`:

- Count the automations to be deleted by paging through `read_automations(offset=...)`, so the confirmation prompt and the final summary report the real total rather than the size of the first page.
- Delete in a loop that re-reads from the start of the collection on every pass instead of collecting ids up front. Deleting shifts the remaining rows, and automations are sorted by name — which is not unique — so deleting by a pre-collected list of offsets could skip or double-delete rows.
- Report the number of automations actually deleted.

### Tests

`tests/events/client/cli/test_automations.py`:

- The `read_automations` and `delete_automation` fixtures now emulate the server: results are paginated at `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT` and deleted automations disappear from subsequent reads. The rest of the file therefore exercises the paged code path.
- `test_deleting_all_automations_across_pages` creates one more automation than the server returns in a single response and asserts that all of them are deleted. Against `main` it fails with `Deleted 200 automations.` and one automation left behind.
- `test_deleting_all_automations_across_unstable_pages` creates automations that share a name — names are not unique, so the server's ordering of same-named automations is not stable across requests — and asserts that every automation is deleted exactly once.

`uv run pytest tests/events/client/cli/test_automations.py` → 48 passed.

A reproduction script is included at `repros/23504.py` (`repros/` is gitignored per the contribution guide). It creates 201 automations and reports how many survive `automation delete --all`:

- against `main`: `Deleted 200 automations.` / `Remaining after automation delete --all: 1`
- against this branch: `Deleted 201 automations.` / `Remaining after automation delete --all: 0`

### Notes

- The prompt and the summary now report the true number of automations instead of the number returned by the first page. This is a user-visible change, but the intent of `--all` is unchanged.
- No documentation update is needed: the CLI reference under `docs/v3/api-ref/cli/` is auto-generated, and no hand-written page documents the behavior of `automation delete --all`.
- The change is scoped to `automations delete --all`; the single-automation delete paths are untouched.

</details>

title: Refresh pip and Conda CA trust in Prefect 2 images
body:
This PR refreshes pip's separate CA bundle and Conda's base environment in Prefect 2 images, then blocks image builds that still trust an affected eMudhra root in the OS, certifi, or pip store. It builds on #23512 and adds an explicit `certifi>=2026.10.19` dependency floor.

**Depends on #23512.** This branch includes its two commits; merge that PR first so this diff shows only the supplemental hardening.

<details>
<summary>Python compatibility and validation</summary>

Python 3.10+ uses patched pip >=26.2.2. No compatible patched pip release is available for Python 3.8/3.9, so those images retain pip 23.3.1 and refresh its vendored CA data from patched certifi before pip makes any network requests. Patched uv 0.13.4 bootstraps these packages. Pip's version metadata is unchanged.

Eight offline regression tests pass on Python 3.8, including the published direct and cross-signed incident chains, each trust store, lazy OpenSSL CA directories, and an isolated pip bundle before and after repair. A targeted Linux Python 3.8 container smoke test and Conda base bootstrap check pass. Pre-commit checks pass with Python 3.11. The dedicated trust-test CI matrix passes on Python 3.8–3.12.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Release scope</summary>

Merging to 2.x does not publish refreshed images. Release/recovery publication must rebuild the intended tags with fresh layers, and the resulting digests must be checked. Existing historical tags remain unchanged until explicitly rebuilt.

No API or usage documentation changes are needed; this updates image trust data and adds publication checks.

</details>

Related: #23512, #23483, #23517 and the [Python advisory](https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576).

- Pre-commit checks pass.

Fixtures are public certificates from the [incident disclosure](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/); verification uses a fixed time to avoid certificate expiration masking trust.

No API or usage documentation changes are needed: this updates image trust data and adds publication checks.

title: Handle unset private attributes during input resolution
body:
closes #23514

This PR lets task input resolution transform Pydantic models whose private attributes have not been initialized. For example, unwrapping a `quote` or completed state in a public field currently fails with `AttributeError` when the model also declares an unset `PrivateAttr()`.

Only copy private attributes that have values. Initialized private values remain untouched, and public fields still use the existing model reconstruction and dependency-resolution logic.

<details>
<summary>Validation and scope</summary>

- The 14 new regression cases fail against unchanged main and pass with the fix.
- Collection traversal and input resolver tests: **130 passed**.
- Related annotation, templating and Pydantic tests: **113 passed**.
- All applicable upstream pre-commit checks passed, including the pinned Ruff lint/format hooks and codespell.
- Tested on Windows / Python 3.12.8 / Pydantic 2.14.1. Full-suite and multi-version CI results are not claimed.

Tests cover unset implicit/explicit private attributes, frozen models, initialized private value identity, unchanged original inputs, and synchronous/asynchronous resolution of both quotes and completed states. No public API or server orchestration changes. This restores supported model input behavior, so separate user documentation is not needed.

Codex assisted with implementation and ran the reproduction/tests against the checkout. These are automated results; no manual human review or manual testing is claimed.

title: Skip unset Pydantic private attributes when rebuilding models in `visit_collection`
body:
closes #23514

This PR fixes task input resolution for Pydantic models that have a private attribute without a value (for example `_cache: dict = PrivateAttr()`).

When `visit_collection` changes a public field, it rebuilds the model with `model_construct` and then copies the private attributes. Before this change, it called `getattr` for each name in `__private_attributes__`. An unset private attribute has no value, so `getattr` raised `AttributeError`, and `resolve_inputs` / `resolve_inputs_sync` raised a `PrefectException`.

Now it copies only the values in `__pydantic_private__`. Pydantic stores private attribute values there, and unset attributes are not in it. Private attributes that have values are copied as before and are not traversed.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `tests/utilities/test_collections.py`: rebuild of mutable and frozen models with no private attributes set, only the implicit `_y` set, and only the explicit `_z` set. Set values are kept; unset attributes stay unset.
- `tests/test_task_engine.py`: sync and async tasks that receive a model with a quoted field and an unset `PrivateAttr()`. These cover `resolve_inputs_sync` and `resolve_inputs`.

All new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. No docs change is necessary because this is a bug fix with no change to the public API.
</details>

title: Read metric triggers on metrics this version doesn't know
body:
Reading an automation with a metric trigger on a metric this client doesn't know now keeps the metric name as a string instead of raising a `ValidationError`.

## The problem

`MetricTriggerQuery.name` is the closed enum `PrefectMetric`: `lateness`, `duration` and `successes`. Prefect Cloud also supports metric triggers on `volume`, `sla_violations` and `sla_violations_by_severity`. Any automation that uses one fails to parse:

```python
Automation.model_validate({..., "trigger": {"type": "metric", "metric": {"name": "volume", ...}}})
# pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Automation
# trigger.metric.metric.name
#   Input should be 'lateness', 'duration' or 'successes' [type=enum, input_value='volume', input_type=str]
```

`read_automations()` parses the whole response at once, so **one such automation breaks the call for the whole workspace**. `prefect automation ls`, `prefect transfer` and `Automation.read()` all fail. This is the trigger-side version of #23426, which did the same for unknown action types. 3.9.0 includes that fix and still fails here.

## The change

- **`MetricTriggerQuery.name` is `Union[PrefectMetric, str]`, validated left to right.** Known names still parse as `PrefectMetric` members, so code that compares against `PrefectMetric` keeps working. An unknown name stays a string.
- **Round trips are lossless.** `Automation.update()` rebuilds an `AutomationCore` from `model_dump()`, and the string survives that, so updating the automation (for example, enabling it) sends the name back unchanged.
- **`describe_for_cli()`** shows an unknown name as is, for example `Metric: volume < 1.0 for 1 day, 0:00:00`.
- **`prefect transfer` skips automations with an unknown metric name**, including one inside a compound or sequence trigger. It reports `TransferSkipped("Uses metrics this version of Prefect does not recognize: ...")` in the results table, as it does for unknown action types. This version can't check whether the destination supports the metric.

### Why a left-to-right union rather than a discriminator

#23426 used a discriminator so that a known action type with invalid fields would still fail validation. A metric name is a bare string with no fields of its own, so there's no invalid known case for a fallback to hide. `union_mode="left_to_right"` keeps known names as enum members. Pydantic's default smart mode would turn them into plain strings.

## Behavior changes to note

- The static type of `MetricTriggerQuery.name` is now `Union[PrefectMetric, str]`. Code that reads `name.value` must handle a string. `isinstance` checks and comparisons with `PrefectMetric` members are unaffected.
- The client no longer catches a misspelled metric name such as `MetricTriggerQuery(name="latness", ...)` before it's sent. The server rejects it on create.
- Clients without this change still fail on these automations. Only clients that include this change benefit.

## Tests

- `tests/events/client/test_automations_schema.py`, `TestUnknownMetricNames`:
  - each of the three metrics parses as a string, and a known name still parses as a `PrefectMetric` member (from Python and from JSON)
  - an unknown metric nested in a sequence inside a compound trigger parses
  - the name survives the `update()` round trip
  - `describe_for_cli()` shows the name
- `tests/cli/transfer/test_automations.py`: transfer skips an automation with unknown metrics in nested triggers, lists them sorted, and doesn't create it.
- The new tests fail without the change, except the known-name test. `tests/events/client`, `tests/cli/transfer` and `tests/test_automations.py` pass (631 tests). Pyright reports no new errors in the changed files.
- Checked against a real Prefect Cloud workspace with a `volume` metric automation. This branch parses the `/automations/filter` response, and 3.9.0 fails on the same response with the error above.

There's no separate issue for this; it's a follow-up to #23426.

title: Drop the eMudhra-compromised CA roots from 2.x images
body:
The published 2.x images still trust two CA roots named in the eMudhra intermediate CA compromise advisory: emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and Comodo AAA Services. Outbound TLS from these images, including client calls to the Prefect API, accepts a certificate for any hostname that the compromised intermediates signed.

Debian has shipped `ca-certificates` updates that remove both roots (`20250419+deb13u1` on trixie, `20250419~deb12u2` on bookworm). The 2.x images do not receive them. The `python:3.8`/`3.9`/`3.10-slim` bases are no longer rebuilt upstream, and the 2.x final stage never runs `apt-get upgrade`. This PR adds that upgrade to the final stage. The 3.x Dockerfile on `main` already does this, and the current 3.x images on Python 3.11+ trust neither root.

certifi needs no change. The eager `pip install --upgrade` already resolves certifi 2026.10.19 on every build, and that release drops both roots.

### Example

Built locally from this branch and from `origin/2.x` on the same day, default flavor unless noted:

| Image | `ca-certificates` | Trusted root links in `/etc/ssl/certs` |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/2.x`, Python 3.10 | `20250419` | 2 |
| this branch, Python 3.10 | `20250419+deb13u1` | 0 |
| this branch, Python 3.8 (bookworm) | `20250419~deb12u2` | 0 |
| this branch, Python 3.10, `-conda` | `20250419+deb13u1` | 0 |

The published `2-latest` image (pushed 2026-09-02) has 2 links and certifi 2026.07.22, which still includes emSign ECC Root CA - G3. In the `-conda` flavor, Python reads conda's own bundle, and conda's `ca-certificates` 2026.10.20 also has neither root. `prefect version` passes in each build.

Not covered: the `git>=1:2.47.3` line in the same `RUN` is unquoted, so the shell reads `>=1:2.47.3` as a redirect and apt installs the distro's git. The bookworm-based Python 3.8 image ships git 2.39.5. That fix belongs in a separate PR.

### Checklist

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
	- No issue exists. This is a small fix.
- [ ] If this pull request adds new functionality, it includes unit tests that cover the changes
	- No new functionality.
- [ ] This pull request includes a label categorizing the change e.g. `maintenance`, `fix`, `feature`, `enhancement`, `docs`.

## Rollout caveats

- `rollout: merging to 2.x publishes nothing.` The image workflow builds on pushes to `main` only, and its recovery dispatch rebuilds an existing tag's own Dockerfile. The fix reaches `prefecthq/prefect` only through a new 2.x release (2.20.27).
- `rollout: older patch tags stay unpatched.` Images such as `2.20.25-python3.10` are never rebuilt. Users pinned to one need to move to the new patch release.
- `watch: build time per matrix cell.` The upgrade adds a package-upgrade step to all 15 cells, including QEMU arm64 builds.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

This came out of customer questions about the eMudhra advisory. We checked the published OSS images: the 3.x images on Python 3.11+ were already clean, and `2-latest` and `3-python3.10` were not. `3-python3.10` is out of the 3.x build matrix, so it is not addressed here. We rejected a distrust `sed` like the one some service images use, because the Debian fix now exists and an upgrade also delivers future security updates.

</details>

title: Fix background worker shutdown hang when worker cancellation is lost
body:
This PR makes `background_worker` shutdown rely on exiting the docket `Worker` context, not just on `worker_task.cancel()`. It fixes the flaky `test_client_runs_migrations_for_two_different_ephemeral_apps[True]` failure on main ([run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39633388366), Python 3.11 only), where the app lifespan shutdown hung until `asgi_lifespan` gave up after 30s.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

On Python 3.11, `asyncio.wait_for` drops a cancellation if the inner future finishes in the same loop iteration. Python 3.12 rewrote `wait_for` and doesn't have this problem. docket's worker calls `wait_for` (through `_wait_for_event`) while it waits for its cancellation listener to start. If an app's lifespan opens and closes right away, as in this test, `worker_task.cancel()` can arrive in that window and get dropped. The worker then keeps running forever, and the old `await worker_task` inside the `Worker` context never returns.

The fix:
- `background_worker` still cancels the task.
- It now waits for the task only after leaving `async with Worker(docket)`. `Worker.__aexit__` sets the worker's stop event and waits for the run loop to finish, so shutdown completes even when the cancellation was dropped.
- If the task never started, cancelling it still keeps it from running.

This also affects real servers running on Python 3.11, not just the tests.

Regression test: `tests/server/api/test_background_workers.py` wraps `Worker.run_forever` so it ignores cancellation, which simulates the dropped cancel. With the old code the test hangs; with this change it passes (20/20 runs on both 3.11 and 3.12). On 3.11, 20 repeat runs of the originally failing test also pass, and the related server and client test modules pass.
</details>

title: Move the remaining Node 20 pins to Node 22
body:
Three Node pins in this repo are still on Node 20. Node 20 is end-of-life, so the October 2026 Node security releases have no fix for it. Advisory: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases

This PR moves all three pins to 22.23.4, the patched release on the 22.x line:

title: Publish duration lower bounds only where validation enforces them
body:
Related to #23400

This PR stops `DurationOrSecondsTimeDelta` from publishing `minimum: 0`. Each field whose validation enforces a lower bound now publishes that bound itself.

**The problem.** #23400 gave `DurationOrSecondsTimeDelta` a JSON Schema with `minimum: 0` on its number branch, in both validation and serialization mode. `CompositeTrigger.within` uses the alias but has no lower bound, so server and client `CompoundTrigger(..., within=-5)` both validate. The server's OpenAPI schema still says `minimum: 0` for that field. A client that validates responses against it would reject an automation the API returned.

**The fix.**
- The alias publishes no bound.
- `EventTrigger.within` publishes `minimum: 0` through `json_schema_extra` in both automations modules. Pydantic leaves a timedelta field's `ge` out of the JSON Schema, so `ge=timedelta(seconds=0)` publishes nothing by itself.
- `NonNegativeTimeDelta` adds its own `WithJsonSchema` pair with the bound. It replaces the alias's pair in both modes, so the three `schedule_after` fields keep publishing `minimum: 0`.
- The client `MetricTriggerQuery.range` and `firing_for` publish `minimum: 300`, which matches `enforce_minimum_range`. Before this PR they published `minimum: 0`.
- `CompositeTrigger.within` stays unbounded in validation. The server reads stored automations back through these models, so adding `ge` would fail reads of any stored automation with a negative `within`.

`docs/v3/api-ref/rest-api/server/schema.json` is regenerated, and its diff contains only these bounds. `ui-v2/src/api/prefect.ts` regenerates with no change, because openapi-typescript does not emit numeric bounds.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

Pydantic 2.10.1, 2.11.5, 2.12.5, 2.13.0, and 2.14.1 all leave a timedelta `ge` out of the schema, and in all of them the outer `WithJsonSchema` pair wins in both modes. On pydantic 2.10.x, `WithJsonSchema` returns its dict without copying it. A field's `default` or `json_schema_extra` is then written into the dict that every field using the alias shares, so another field's `minimum` can appear on `CompositeTrigger.within` depending on generation order. Main publishes it there on every version, and 2.10 already leaks field defaults the same way. Pydantic 2.11 copies the dict, and CI does not test 2.10. Raising the floor to 2.11.5 is left for a separate change.

The `CompositeTrigger.within` and alias tests fail on main. The bound tests pass on main, because main publishes the bound everywhere. They fail when the `json_schema_extra` lines and the `NonNegativeTimeDelta` pair are removed.

</details>

title: Delete every automation with `prefect automation delete --all`
body:
closes #23504

this PR makes `prefect automation delete --all` delete every automation instead of only the first page that `read_automations()` returns (`PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, 200 by default). The confirmation prompt and the final message now show the real count.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The change uses the same approach as `prefect deployment delete --all` (#23440) and the bulk-read contract in `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`:

- The confirmation count pages through `read_automations(offset=...)` until it gets an empty page.
- Deletion reads the first page, deletes it (still with at most 10 concurrent deletes), and repeats until no automations remain. Reading from offset 0 each time does not skip rows that move into earlier pages after a delete, and does not depend on a stable sort order.
- `Deleted N automations.` reports the number that the command actually deleted.

Tests: the new `paged_automation_store` fixture serves copies of the mocked automations with distinct ids. On `main`, both tests fail: the prompt asks about 2 automations and only 2 are deleted. With this change, they pass.

Manual check against a local server: I created 205 automations and ran `prefect --no-prompt automation delete --all`. The command printed `Deleted 205 automations.` and 0 automations remained.

Alternative to #23505.
</details>

title: Remove direct dependency on ruamel.yaml.clib
body:
this PR removes Prefect's direct dependency on `ruamel.yaml.clib`, which has no cp315 wheels and breaks the `prefect-client` Python 3.15 Docker build, and pins `ruamel.yaml` to exclude 0.19.0 (the one release that requires `ruamel.yaml.clibz`).

<details>

The 3.9.0 release run of the "Docker images" workflow failed on "Build and publish to DockerHub (prefecthq/prefect-client, 3.15)": https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39529569042/job/118992111168

`ruamel.yaml.clib` 0.2.15 has no cp315 wheels, so `uv pip install` tried to build it from source and failed because `client/Dockerfile` has no C compiler (`error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'gcc'`). Upstream has moved to `ruamel.yaml.clibz` and is not expected to publish 3.15 wheels for `clib`.

The direct `clib` dependency was added in #20068 when `ruamel.yaml` 0.19.0 required `ruamel.yaml.clibz` (which needs Zig to compile). Since 0.19.1, both extensions are optional extras, so a plain `ruamel.yaml` install is pure Python. Prefect's only use is `YAML()` with the default round-trip loader in `src/prefect/deployments/base.py`, which doesn't use the C extension.

Changes:
- `pyproject.toml` and `client/pyproject.toml`: removed `"ruamel.yaml.clib>=0.2.8; platform_python_implementation == 'CPython'"` and changed the pin to `"ruamel.yaml>=0.17.0,!=0.19.0"`.
- Regenerated `uv.lock` with `uv lock`.

Verified locally:
- `docker build --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.15 -f client/Dockerfile` succeeds; the image contains `ruamel-yaml 0.19.1` and no `ruamel.yaml.clib`/`clibz`.
- `docker build --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.11 -f client/Dockerfile` still succeeds.
- `uv run pytest tests/deployment/ tests/cli/test_deploy.py -n4`: 386 passed, 1 skipped.

</details>

title: Remove deprecated Runner execution paths
body:
Related to #21252

**The problem.** `Runner.execute_flow_run`, `Runner.execute_bundle` and `Runner.reschedule_current_flow_runs` were deprecated in 3.6.24 (#21252), and the deprecation message promised removal after Sep 2026. Their private code was a second execution path next to `FlowRunExecutor`, with its own process map, kill logic, crash handling and cancellation branch.

**The change.** This PR removes the three methods and the private code that only they used. `Runner._cancel_run` now only delegates to `CancellationManager` for runs that `ProcessManager` tracks.

`ProcessWorker._submit_adhoc_run` was the last internal caller. It now opens a `FlowRunExecutorContext` with `BundleExecutionStarter` and `propose_submitting=False`, the same way `ProcessWorker.run` does. The worker no longer creates a `Runner`.

The runner webserver's `/run_count` read the removed process map. That map was empty for served runs, so the endpoint always returned 0. It now reads `ProcessManager.flow_run_count()`, which takes the map's length without iterating it, because the endpoint runs on the webserver thread.

## Breaking change

Code that ignored the deprecation warnings and still calls these methods now fails with `AttributeError`:

- `Runner.execute_flow_run`: use `FlowRunExecutorContext` with a `ProcessStarter`, such as `WorkspaceResolvingEngineCommandStarter`.
- `Runner.execute_bundle`: use `execute_bundle()` from `prefect.bundles.execute`.
- `Runner.reschedule_current_flow_runs`: no replacement. `prefect flow-run execute` handles SIGTERM rescheduling.

title: Preserve replacement text within each templating pass

This PR substitutes only the placeholders present in the input to each `apply_values` call. Replacement text is left for a later explicit pass. Seven independent runtime controls cover repeated/spacing variants, skipped prefixes, missing values, typed whole-string values, environment text and a second explicit pass. Applicable pre-commit/pre-push hooks pass.

title: Substitute `apply_values` placeholders in a single pass
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23491

this PR makes `apply_values` resolve every placeholder in a string and then substitute them into the original template in one `PLACEHOLDER_CAPTURE_REGEX.sub` pass. Previously each placeholder was applied with sequential `str.replace` calls over a `set`, so a value that contained placeholder syntax could be substituted again, and the result depended on `PYTHONHASHSEED`.

<details>

```python
apply_values("prefix {{ first }} / {{ second }}", {"first": "{{ second }}", "second": "resolved"})
# before: "prefix {{ second }} / resolved" or "prefix resolved / resolved" depending on hash seed
# after:  "prefix {{ second }} / resolved" always
```

Unchanged: whole-string typed replacement, `skip_prefixes`, block/variable placeholders left for later resolution, `remove_notset`/`warn_on_notset` handling (still one warning per unique placeholder), and the explicit multi-pass pipeline in deployment steps.

title: docs: document _pendulum_call convention for Python 3.11–3.12 datetimes
body:
this PR adds one Key Contracts bullet to `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`. The bullet says that internal Prefect code on Python 3.11–3.12 must call Pendulum-only datetime members through `_pendulum_call`, because calling them directly sends deprecation warnings to users. It follows #23328, which deprecated Pendulum datetime behavior.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "On Python 3.11–3.12, call Pendulum-only members through `_pendulum_call`." On those versions, Prefect's `DateTime`/`Date`/`Duration` emit a `DeprecationWarning` from Pendulum-specific methods (`add`, `in_tz`, `naive`, `end_of`, `diff_for_humans`, ...) and from `replace`/`now`-style shared methods. Internal code must use `_pendulum_call(obj, "name", ...)` from `types/_datetime.py`. The pytest config ignores `Pendulum datetime member` warnings globally, so the test suite will not catch a direct call.
Non-obvious evidence: `pyproject.toml` `filterwarnings` includes `ignore:Pendulum datetime member:DeprecationWarning`, so a new direct `dt.add(...)`/`dt.in_tz(...)` in Prefect code passes CI and still warns end users. The only regression guard is a subprocess test that checks `import prefect` itself. I checked on Python 3.12 that `add`/`naive`/`end_of`/`replace` warn and `_pendulum_call(...)` stays silent.
Cross-cutting scope: Applies anywhere under `src/prefect/` that works with Prefect datetimes: server schedules, the UI API, runtime, the deprecation utilities, and `types/_datetime.py` helpers. #23328 had to update all of these call sites.
Why not code comment/docstring: The `_pendulum_call` docstring only describes what the function does. Anyone adding a new call site in another module never reads that docstring, and the test filter that hides the mistake lives in `pyproject.toml`. The rule sits next to the existing datetime-helper contract for 3.13+.
Durability: The deprecation period runs for at least six months and three minor releases, and every new datetime call site during that time is exposed. Remove the bullet together with `_datetime_deprecations.py`.
Counter-evidence checked: Existing `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` datetime bullet (3.13+/whenever only), `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`, `tests/AGENTS.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, `_datetime_deprecations.py` module docstring, `_pendulum_call` docstring, `tests/test_datetime.py`, `pyproject.toml` filterwarnings.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in triggering push (79ff36f2..46a76c25)</summary>

- pyproject.toml

- src/prefect/_internal/compatibility/deprecated.py

title: Update certifi and uv for eMudhra CA compromise
body:
This PR requires `certifi>=2026.10.19` and updates `uv` to `0.13.4` to remove trust paths affected by the [eMudhra intermediate CA compromise](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/).

<details>
<summary>Details and checks</summary>

- Applies the `certifi` requirement to both `prefect` and `prefect-client`.
- Updates the `uv` dependency floors, Docker pins, pre-commit hook, and proxy-test pin. Only `certifi` and `uv` versions change in the lockfile.
- Refreshes six lines of generated deployment settings types required by the OpenAPI pre-push hook, in a separate commit.
- Passes 31 focused TLS/WebSocket/subscription tests, 8 interval-schedule UI tests, and the UI production build.
- Checks the lockfile and Docker dependency export. The installed `certifi` rejects all 12 published compromised chains offline, and `uv` rejects both published test hosts with certificate errors.

No application logic changes or additional API documentation are needed for these dependency updates. Existing tests and explicit certificate checks cover the affected behavior.

</details>

Note: Published images and existing installations still need rebuilding or updating and restarting to receive the fixes. System CA stores and Node updates require separate follow-up.

title: fix(server/schemas/filters): include combined any_/not_any_ filters in FlowRunFilterState
body:
## Summary of Changes
The `FlowRunFilterState._get_filter_list` method was filtering out combined `any_` and `not_any_` filters because it only appended results that were instances of `sqlalchemy.BinaryExpression`. When both `any_` and `not_any_` are set, the filter returns a `BooleanClauseList` (from `sa.and_`), which was incorrectly skipped. This caused the server to return flow runs that should have been excluded. The fix changes the condition to accept any filter that is not `sa.true()` (the default when no filters are present), ensuring combined filters are included.

## Motivation & Context
Closes #23458

## Verification
The fix can be verified by running the reproduction script from the issue, which should now return only the Completed run when filtering with `any_=["COMPLETED", "FAILED"]` and `not_any_=["FAILED"]`.
- Gate Report: Python syntax compiled: src/prefect/server/schemas/filters.py; Notice: Python tests had failures in tests/

title: Reinstall UI deps in Docker build when npm drops native Vite bindings
body:
This PR makes the `ui-builder` and `ui-v2-builder` Docker stages check that the native bindings for Vite (`lightningcss` and `rolldown`) load after `npm ci`. If they do not load, the stage runs `npm ci` one more time. Then it checks again and stops the build if the bindings still do not load.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

The `docker, python:3.11` job in [Unit tests run 39479980329](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39479980329) failed in `[ui-builder 7/7] RUN npm run build`:

```
[lightningcss minify] Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'
Require stack:
- /opt/ui/node_modules/lightningcss/node/index.js
```

The commit (598010268b) changes no UI files. The run before it on main (39479916409) has the same `ui/` lockfile and passed. In that passing run, `npm ci` reported `added 553 packages`. In the failed run it reported `added 552 packages`. The one missing package is `lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu`.

npm treats failures in optional dependencies as non-fatal. In arborist, `[_handleOptionalFailure]` puts the failed package in the trash list and only logs `failed optional dependency` at verbose level. The platform-specific native bindings are optional dependencies. So a temporary download or extract failure lets `npm ci` exit 0 without the binding, and the error only appears later in `vite build`.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- `docker build --target ui-builder --build-arg NODE_VERSION=24.20.0 .` and `docker build --target ui-v2-builder .` pass.
- In the built `ui-builder` image, I removed `node_modules/lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu`. The check failed, the second `npm ci` installed the binding again, and `npm run build` passed.
</details>

### Checklist

  - If no issue exists and your change is not a small fix, please [create an issue](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/new/choose) first.

title: Cap fastapi below 0.151
body:
Caps FastAPI below 0.151 in `pyproject.toml` and `client/pyproject.toml`, and locks it to 0.150.0.

FastAPI 0.151.0 ([fastapi/fastapi#16536](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16536)) validates an explicit JSON `null` against a body parameter instead of using the parameter's default. The client sends `null` for unset `sort`, `limit` and filters, so on 0.151 and later about 144 body parameters across 55 server endpoints return 422: most `/filter`, `/count`, `/paginate` and `/history` routes, which break `read_flow_runs`, `prefect deploy`, worker heartbeats and artifact and log reads. A fresh install currently resolves FastAPI 0.155, so it hits this. The cap comes off once the server treats `null` as the default again; that work is tracked separately.

Two smaller changes between 0.141 and 0.150 also needed fixes:

- 0.145 removed `FastAPI.extra`, which browser `prefect cloud login` used to pass state between the login server and the CLI. It now uses the app's `state`.
- 0.148 stopped validating omitted query defaults, so the flow-run graph's `since` default reached the handler as a string. The default is now the datetime itself.

The existing cloud-login and flow-run-graph tests fail on 0.150 without these fixes and pass with them. The server, client, runner, worker and CLI suites pass on 0.150.0 (4,233 passed).

title: Wait for the events client to confirm events before asserting in checkpoint tests
body:
`test_background_checkpoint_reconnects_after_connection_loss[PrefectCloudEventsClient]` failed on CI with `assert 1 == 0`: the client still held one unconfirmed event. The test kills the connection after the event arrives, then sleeps a fixed 0.5s and asserts the background checkpoint has reconnected, resent the event, and confirmed it. In the failing run, asyncio logged `Executing <Task ... PrefectEventsClient._checkpoint_loop() running at clients.py:502 ...> took 0.809 seconds`: an event-loop stall on the busy runner outlasted the sleep, so the assertion ran before the reconnect finished. The client behaved correctly.

This replaces the fixed sleeps with a helper that polls until the client holds no unconfirmed events, for up to 5 seconds, and then lets the existing assertion report the result. Two sibling tests used the same sleep-then-assert pattern (`test_background_checkpoint_clears_unconfirmed_events`, `test_background_checkpoint_retries_reconnect_until_server_available`) and get the same change. No assertion changes.

Verification: forcing a 0.6s stall inside `_reconnect` reproduces the CI failure 40 of 40 runs before this change and passes 120 of 120 after (with the two sibling tests, at 0.6s and 1.5s stalls). With the client's reconnect disabled, the test still fails after the 5s wait. `tests/events/client/` passes (430).

title: Use min_length and max_length on request bodies so the server imports on FastAPI 0.155
body:
FastAPI 0.155.0 (released 2026-10-20) removed the deprecated catch-all `**extra` from `Path`, `Query`, `Header`, `Cookie`, `Body`, `Form` and `File`, so an unknown keyword now raises `TypeError`. Six request parameters in the server API passed keywords FastAPI never had, so on a fresh install that resolves FastAPI 0.155, `prefect.server.api` fails to import:

```
TypeError: Body() got an unexpected keyword argument 'min_items'
```

This switches them to the keywords FastAPI does have:

- `min_items=1` to `min_length=1` on `names` for `POST /v2/concurrency_limits/increment`, `/increment-with-lease` and `/decrement`
- `max_items=200` to `max_length=200` on the id lists for `POST /ui/flow_runs/count-task-runs`, `/ui/flows/count-deployments` and `/ui/flows/next-runs`

On FastAPI before 0.155 the old keywords were never validated. They were copied into the OpenAPI schema as non-standard `min_items`/`max_items` keys and nothing else, so the new keywords start enforcing limits that were only documented:

- An empty `names` now returns 422 on the three concurrency slot endpoints. Before, it returned 200; on `increment-with-lease` it created a lease that held no limits. The SDK's `concurrency()` and `rate_limit()` return early on empty names (since #14789), so they never send one, but a direct `client.increment_concurrency_slots([])` or `client.release_concurrency_slots([])` now raises.
- More than 200 ids now returns 422 on the three UI routes. The UIs send at most one page of ids (the server caps pages at `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, 200 by default) or batch them at 200.

`tests/server/api/test_fastapi_param_keywords.py` checks every FastAPI request-parameter call in `src/prefect/` against the function's real signature. CI runs the locked FastAPI 0.141.1, which accepts unknown keywords without a warning, so without it the next one would pass CI and fail installs. The regenerated `docs/v3/api-ref/rest-api/server/schema.json` changes only these six fields, now standard `minItems`/`maxItems`.

There is no linked issue: this fixes an import failure on the current FastAPI release.

title: Cut CPU spent delivering events and API logs
body:
closes #23472

This PR cuts the CPU a flow run spends sending events and API logs to the API: 66% less for logs and 45% less for events, with lower peak memory under log load.

Queue services now take an item directly when one is already queued, and wait on the queue thread only when the queue is empty. A service working through a backlog yields to the global event loop every 256 items. `APILogWorker.send` serializes each log with orjson and queues only the bytes, and `_handle_batch` posts them joined to `/logs/`.

| Workload, median of 3 runs | CPU before → after | Peak RSS growth before → after |
|---|---|---|
| 20,000 run-logger lines | 1.43 s → 0.49 s | +16.2 MB → +12.2 MB |
| 5,000 `emit_event` calls in one flow | 0.78 s → 0.43 s | +7.9 MB → +7.9 MB |

Every log and event reached the server in every run. I measured against a local `prefect server start` on SQLite, on macOS with Python 3.14.

Behavior changes for review:

- `APILogWorker` is now `BatchedQueueService[bytes]`. `send()` still accepts dicts. A subclass that overrides `_handle_batch` or `_get_size` now receives bytes.
- `__payload_size__` values are smaller, because orjson writes compact UTF-8. httpx 0.28 already sent compact UTF-8, so request bodies are unchanged. Truncation still keeps each log within `PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_MAX_LOG_SIZE`.
- A message with a lone surrogate now fails in `prepare()`, and only that log is dropped. Before, httpx failed to encode the request and dropped the whole batch.
- When `PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_BATCH_SIZE` is less than twice `PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_MAX_LOG_SIZE`, batches now hold fewer logs, so each request stays within the batch size. The defaults (4,000,000 and 1,000,000, or 25,000 on Prefect Cloud) are not affected.

No docs change: settings and documented behavior are unchanged.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
- [x] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`.
- [x] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

This came out of a prototype that compared three ways to deliver events and logs: the current Python services, a Python-only fix, and a Rust background thread. This PR is the Python-only fix, rebuilt with tests.

Logs are serialized twice with orjson: once in `prepare()` to measure and truncate, and once in `send()`. If the bytes from `prepare()` rode along in its dict, a subclass or a process-pool message processor that changes the dict afterward would cause stale JSON to be posted. The second pass costs about 0.1 µs per log.

The prototype raised peak memory under log load. The cause is orjson's output: each result kept about 1 KiB of memory even for a 250-byte log, so 20,000 queued logs grew RSS by 27.5 MB. Copying each result to an exact-size bytes object brings that to 6.1 MB. I measured this only on macOS.

</details>

title: fix(server): begin SQLite write transaction before reading automation buckets
body:
closes #23470

This PR makes `reactive_evaluation` start its transaction with the write lock on SQLite, so concurrent events no longer fail with `database is locked` when they update an automation bucket.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Some trigger paths read bucket state before they write it. For example, an `expect` event for a trigger with `after` calls `read_bucket` and then `increment_bucket`. On SQLite, the transaction starts as `BEGIN DEFERRED`. If another connection commits between the read and the write, SQLite cannot upgrade the transaction and fails immediately with `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` ("database is locked"). The busy timeout does not apply to this error.

Changes:
- `automations_session` now accepts `with_for_update` and passes it to `db.session_context`.
- `reactive_evaluation` uses `automations_session(begin_transaction=True, with_for_update=True)`. On SQLite this emits `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so the transaction waits for the write lock (with the busy timeout) before it reads. On Postgres, `with_for_update` has no effect on the transaction begin, so behavior does not change.

This is the same approach as #23052 (`mark_deployments_ready`).

The new test `test_concurrent_bucket_updates_count_each_event_once` opens a bucket with an `after` event, then evaluates 25 `expect` events concurrently. It checks that the bucket count is exactly 25 (no lost or double-counted events). Without the fix, the test fails on SQLite with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`.
</details>
