Found this case during when the agent wrote a similar code like the one below. 
Different tasks can then get the same cache key, causing one task to return another’s saved result.
Fixed by hashing the complete code object.

```python
from prefect import flow, task

# These might come from a database or YAML configuration.
customer_rules = {
    "standard_customer": 1,
    "enterprise_customer": 100,
}


def create_pricing_task(customer, fee):
    namespace = {}
    exec(
        f"def calculate_total(amount):\n"
        f"    return amount + {fee}\n",
        namespace,
    )
    return task(name=f"price-{customer}", persist_result=True)(
        namespace["calculate_total"]
    )


standard_price = create_pricing_task(
    "standard_customer", customer_rules["standard_customer"]
)
enterprise_price = create_pricing_task(
    "enterprise_customer", customer_rules["enterprise_customer"]
)


@flow
def generate_invoices():
    standard = standard_price(10, return_state=True)
    enterprise = enterprise_price(10, return_state=True)

    print(f"Standard invoice:   ${standard.result()} ({standard.name})")
    print(f"Enterprise invoice: ${enterprise.result()} ({enterprise.name})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    generate_invoices()
```

Expected:

```text
Standard invoice:   $11 (Completed)
Enterprise invoice: $110 (Completed)
```

With the bug:

```text
Standard invoice:   $11 (Completed)
Enterprise invoice: $11 (Cached)
```

title: Fix forked children exiting with code 1 after a QueueService started
body:
closes #23463

A process forked after a `QueueService` started (e.g. PyTorch `DataLoader` workers inside a flow run) always exits with code 1. `start()` registers `_at_exit` with `threading._register_atexit`; in the child, `reset_for_fork()` sets `_done_event = None` but the callback stays registered, so at shutdown `drain(at_exit=True)` → `_drain()` hits `assert self._done_event is not None`, and `multiprocessing` turns that into exit code 1.

**Fix:** `_drain()` treats `_done_event is None` the same as an already-set event and returns a completed future (`False`). In that state the service never ran in the current process, so there is nothing to wait for. `_stop()` is already a no-op there because `reset_for_fork()` sets `_stopped = True`.

I chose this over removing the callback from `threading._threading_atexits` in `reset_for_fork()` (the other option in the issue) because it doesn't touch another private `threading` internal and also covers `drain()` called directly on a reset service.

**Tests** (`tests/_internal/concurrency/test_services.py`):
- `test_drain_after_reset_for_fork_does_not_fail`: after `reset_for_fork()`, `drain(at_exit=True)` returns `False` and `_at_exit()` doesn't raise (runs on every platform)
- `test_forked_child_exits_cleanly_after_service_started`: a `fork` child of a process with a started service exits with 0 (skipped without `os.fork`)

Both fail on `main` and pass with the change. Run on Linux (`python:3.12-slim`, `uv sync --group dev`): `test_services.py` 44 passed; `tests/_internal/concurrency` + `tests/events/client/test_bounded_queue.py` 188 passed, 2 skipped. The reproduction script from the issue prints `child exitcode 0` with the change (`1` on `main`). `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (v0.15.19, as pinned in pre-commit) pass on both files.

*AI disclosure: I used Claude to help investigate and draft this change and the tests; I reviewed the result and validated it locally as described above.*

title: Keep the patched test clock timezone-aware on Python 3.12
body:
Follows #23445.

On Python 3.11 and 3.12, `prefect.types._datetime.DateTime` is pendulum's. The `frozen_time` and `advance_time` fixtures returned `now(tz)` as a pendulum datetime with a plain `ZoneInfo` tzinfo, and pendulum drops that tzinfo on arithmetic. Both fixtures now convert through `create_datetime_instance`, the same path the real `now(tz)` uses, so the patched clock returns the same kind of object. A new test in `tests/fixtures/test_time.py` checks both fixtures. The lost-follower test in #23445 goes back to using `advance_time`.

Found while fixing CI on #23445. That PR worked around it by patching `now` inside the one test. This PR fixes the fixtures instead, so other tests that subtract from the patched clock on 3.11 and 3.12 get aware times too.

title: Fix forked child processes exiting with code 1 because of QueueService at-exit drain
body:
closes #23463

This PR makes `_QueueServiceBase._drain` return immediately when `_done_event` is `None`. This is the state after `reset_for_fork`, or when the service did not start in this process.

This makes PyTorch `DataLoader` workers fail inside flow runs.

Now `_drain` returns a completed future (`False`) in this state. This is the same result as for a service that is already done.

- `test_forked_child_exits_cleanly_with_running_service`: a forked child exits with code 0 while a service runs in the parent. This test fails without the fix.
- `test_multiprocessing_after_test_harness` used `os._exit(0)` in its worker to avoid this bug. The worker now returns normally. This test also fails without the fix.

Repro script from the issue: child exit code goes from 1 to 0.
</details>

title: Apply both `any_` and `not_any_` in flow run state filters
body:
Closes #23458

This PR makes a flow run state filter apply when its type or name part sets both `any_` and `not_any_`. Before, the state criteria were dropped and every flow run matched: with a Completed run and a Failed run, `any_=["COMPLETED", "FAILED"]` with `not_any_=["FAILED"]` returned both.

<details>
<summary>Cause, test and range</summary>

`FlowRunFilterState._get_filter_list` kept the `as_sql_filter()` result of its type and name parts only if it was a `BinaryExpression` ([filters.py](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/1c866f04d6268a56a02bdbc1f8aa4b1788c39f89/src/prefect/server/schemas/filters.py#L429-L436)). The fix skips a part only when it sets nothing (`sa.true()`), so each part stays one group: with `operator="or_"`, spreading its two comparisons into the outer `or_` would match every flow run. `TaskRunFilterState` has the same check, but its parts only have `any_`, so it is not affected.

title: Filter Kubernetes observer LIST/WATCH server-side and page initial lists
body:
closes #22208

This PR makes the Kubernetes worker observer ask the API server only for Prefect-labeled pods and jobs, and splits the initial LIST into pages of 500. Before this change, kopf listed and watched every pod and job in scope and filtered them client-side.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `configure` (the kopf startup handler) now sets `settings.watching.label_selectors` for `("v1", "pods")` and `("batch", "v1", "jobs")`, and sets `settings.watching.chunk_size = 500`. These settings were added in [kopf 1.45](https://github.com/nolar/kopf/releases/tag/1.45.0) ([nolar/kopf#1311](https://github.com/nolar/kopf/pull/1311)). kopf applies them to the initial LIST and to the WATCH that follows, for both namespaced and cluster-wide URLs. Namespace and CRD discovery are not filtered.
- The selector comes from the existing filter definition. `_pod_label_filters`/`_pod_label_selector` are renamed to `_observed_label_filters`/`_observed_label_selector`. The pod handler, the job crash handler (which used to build its own copy of the mapping), pod lifecycle reconciliation, and the server-side selector all use them now. The default is presence of `prefect.io/flow-run-id`. `additional_label_filters` are merged in afterward with the same precedence as before, and an empty value renders as `key=` (equality), not presence.
- With a server-side selector, Kubernetes reports a job whose labels stop matching (for example, an `additional_label_filters` value changed or the `prefect.io/flow-run-id` label removed) as `DELETED` with its old body, even though the job still exists. Before treating a `DELETED` event as a deletion, `_mark_flow_run_as_crashed` now reads the job by namespace and name with `_job_still_exists`:
  - A 404, or a job with a different UID (a replacement), confirms the deletion. The handler then re-reads the flow run, re-applies the terminal, cancelling, paused and scheduled checks, and continues into the existing replacement-job wait. That wait now excludes the deleted job by UID rather than by name, so a replacement that reuses the name keeps the run alive.
  - The same UID means the job only left the selector, so the handler skips without proposing `Crashed`.
  - kopf runs `@kopf.on.event` handlers once, with no retry. So transient lookup failures (408, 429, any 5xx except 501, timeouts, connection errors) are retried in place with capped exponential backoff and jitter (1s up to 60s). Each request has a 30s timeout, so a hung request becomes a retry. Retries continue until the lookup gives a definite answer or kopf cancels the handler. Each attempt opens and closes its own API client.
  - Permanent errors (for example 401/403/422/501) log a warning and leave the flow run alone. A failed lookup never counts as proof that the job is gone.
  - The label-filtered job LIST isn't used to decide whether a job was deleted, because it can't see a job whose flow run label was removed.
- No field selectors, and `initial_streaming` keeps its default. Terminal pods (`Succeeded`/`Failed`) and failed jobs still reach the handlers, so terminal pod events and crash detection don't change.
- The `kopf` floor goes from `>=1.37.4` to `>=1.45.1`. `uv lock --upgrade-package kopf` moves the root lock from 1.40.0 to 1.45.1. The only other lock change is kopf's new `jsonpatch` dependency edge, and `jsonpatch` was already in the lock.

New tests in `tests/test_observer.py::TestServerSideFiltering`:
- They pass a real `kopf.OperatorSettings` through `configure` and check that pods and jobs get the selector while namespaces and CRDs don't. This covers the default filter, extra filters with an empty value, and an override of the default key. They also check `chunk_size == 500`, no field selectors, and `initial_streaming` still off.
- A boundary test runs kopf 1.45.1's real `fetch_objs`/`watch_objs` against a local aiohttp fake of the Kubernetes API. For pods and jobs, namespaced and cluster-wide, it checks the requests: both LIST pages carry `limit=500` and the `labelSelector` (the second with the `continue` token), and the WATCH carries the same `labelSelector`.

New tests in `TestMarkFlowRunAsCrashed` replace the Kubernetes client's `read_namespaced_job` call with a test double. They cover:
- a still-active, same-UID job that leaves the selector, through a changed equality label or a removed flow run label: no `Crashed`;
- a job recreated under the same name with a new UID: `Crashed` if the replacement isn't active, no `Crashed` if the job LIST shows it running;
- a transient failure (503, 429, 520, timeout, connection error) followed by a 404: `Crashed` once, with no second watch event;
- 50 consecutive 503s followed by a 404: still crashes;
- a timeout followed by the same UID: no `Crashed`;
- a flow that becomes `Cancelling` or `Completed` while the lookup is retrying: no `Crashed`;
- cancelling the handler during a retry wait: it stops immediately and closes the client;
- permanent errors (including 501): no retry and no `Crashed`.

`uv run --no-sources pytest tests/test_observer.py tests/test_settings.py` passes: 140 tests.

This lowers how much the API server sends and how much one LIST response holds. It does not set a fixed limit on worker memory: kopf still keeps per-object state for every matching pod and job that is retained.

</details>

title: Resolve numeric string dict keys in `get_from_dict`
body:
closes #23452

This PR changes `get_from_dict` so that a string path segment finds a string dictionary key with the same value. Before this change, `get_from_dict` changed each segment to an `int` before the lookup. Thus `{"years": {"2026": 42}}` with the path `years.2026` returned the default value, and `apply_values` removed the templated field.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

For each segment, the lookup now depends on the container type:

- **Mapping:** use the exact key if it is in the mapping. If it is not, change the key to an `int` only when the string is a canonical integer (`"1"`, `"-1"`). Strings such as `"01"` stay as strings, because `str(int("01")) != "01"`.
- **Other containers (lists, tuples):** no change. The segment is changed to an `int` when possible, so `a.1`, `a[1]`, `a[-1]`, and `a.-1` work as before.

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `get_from_dict({"years": {"2026": 42}}, "years.2026")` | `None` | `42` |
| `apply_values({"year": "{{ years.2026 }}"}, {"years": {"2026": 42}})` | `{}` | `{"year": 42}` |
| `get_from_dict({"items": {"01": "first"}}, "items.01")` | `None` | `"first"` |
| `get_from_dict({"a": {1: "int", "1": "str"}}, "a.1")` | `"int"` | `"str"` |
| `get_from_dict({"a": {1: "int"}}, "a.1")` | `"int"` | `"int"` |

One small change in behavior: `get_from_dict({"a": {1: "x"}}, "a.01")` now returns the default value, not `"x"`. The issue asks for this, because `"01"` identifies a string key.

`set_in_dict` already uses string segments as they are, so `set_in_dict` and `get_from_dict` now agree on paths with numeric string keys.

Tests: new parametrized cases in `tests/utilities/test_collections.py::TestGetFromDict` and a new `apply_values` test in `tests/utilities/test_templating.py`. `uv run pytest tests/utilities/test_collections.py tests/utilities/test_templating.py` passes (203 tests).

Docs: the `get_from_dict` docstring describes the new lookup order. No other documentation update is necessary.
</details>

title: Fix numeric string key lookup in get_from_dict
body:
Closes #23452

This PR lets get_from_dict resolve numeric string dictionary keys before trying
an integer key or sequence index. For example, apply_values now preserves and
resolves {"year": "{{ years.2026 }}"} with {"years": {"2026": 42}} instead of
silently returning an empty dictionary.

<details>
<summary>Approach and validation</summary>

The lookup tries the original key first. If that raises TypeError or KeyError,
it tries an integer key, preserving integer-only dictionaries and existing
dotted/bracketed list indexing, including negative indices and tuples. When
both 1 and "1" are present, a string path selects "1"; an explicit integer
component in a key list still selects 1. Falsy values do not trigger fallback.
The function docstring describes this precedence.
The priority choice for `{1: "int", "1": "str"}` accessed through `a.1` can be adjusted in response to maintainer feedback.

Only collection lookup changes. Template removal behavior and NotSet are
